The report said the federal government believed the acquisition would represent a “net conservation benefit” and provide “substantial long-term conservation value and improving landscape-scale habitat connectivity across refuges in south Texas”.The judge said that the plaintiffs offered “relatively weak” evidence of environmental harm.“While they rightfully argue that the preservation of wildlife and historical lands furthers the public interest, they present no evidence demonstrating that the Property will suffer aesthetic, environmental, cultural, or historical degradation during the pendency of this lawsuit,” Rodriguez wrote in his ruling.In addition, the judge said a preliminary injunction would result in modifications to SpaceX’s development plans, “placing additional hardship on the company’s ability to meet milestones and contractual obligations”.SpaceX did not return an email seeking comment on the judge’s ruling.The space exploration company first broke ground in Texas more than a decade ago and has expanded rapidly, so much that SpaceX employees last year voted to incorporate their own local government called Starbase.Explore more on these topicsTrump administrationSpaceXTexasUS politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Plan for editorial oversight board at CNN and CBS News draws skepticism: ‘Utter garbage’ | CNN | The Guardian
description: Some network employees and media-watchers have questions and concerns about how arrangement will work
Author: Jeremy Barr
Headline: Some network employees and media-watchers have questions and concerns about how arrangement will work
Content: An editorial oversight board must be set up within 180 days after the closing of the merger deal between Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery.Photograph: Kevin Carter/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAn editorial oversight board must be set up within 180 days after the closing of the merger deal between Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery.Photograph: Kevin Carter/Getty ImagesCNNPlan for editorial oversight board at CNN and CBS News draws skepticism: ‘Utter garbage’Some network employees and media-watchers have questions and concerns about how arrangement will workJeremy Barrin WashingtonMon 21 Sep 2026 16.05 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 16.24 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLeading media figures and insiders dismissed plans to create an editorial oversight board to protectCNN’s independence as “utter garbage” – in one staffer’s words – after a settlement was reached to resolve a lawsuit filed by a coalition of 12 states to blockParamount’s $110bn acquisition ofWarner Bros Discovery.California’s attorney general, Rob Bonta, during a press conference to announce the settlement, said that Paramount “must establish a news editorial independence board to supportCBSNews and CNN’s continued editorial independence to ensure independent, objective, fact-based reporting at CBS News and at CNN”.In a legal motion to formally end the case, the companies said the news editorial independence board would “establish guiding editorial and journalism principles for the combined entity’s news channels”.Paramount settles lawsuits with 12 US states, clearing way for Warner mergerRead moreAccording to the terms of the settlement, the board must be established within 180 days of the closing of the deal. It will be composed of five current or former journalists with at least 10 years of experience each and will be appointed by the board of the company for three-year terms.The board will be tasked with “resolving any disputes between CBS News employees,CNNemployees and management of the combined entity regarding alleged violations of the news editorial principles”; “resolving any disputes between CBS News employees, CNN employees and management of the combined entity regarding alleged reporting bias or failure to meet agreed reporting fairness standards”; and “establishing and monitoring adherence to ethical journalism as defined by journalism industry best practices and to editorial independence, including from the combined entity’s ownership and shareholders”.Critics of the mega-merger had expressed concerns about CNN being taken over by the Ellison family, which has well-documented connections to the Trump administration.David Ellisonandhis father, Larry Ellison, have reportedly spoken with the White House about potential changes they might make at CNN, which could ultimately generate more positive coverage of the Trump administration, a prospect that has worried journalists at the cable news network.On Monday afternoon, there was already some skepticism within the media industry – including from current and former employees at the companies involved in the deal – about whether the editorial oversight board would actually protect CNN’s editorial integrity.“There is no way that is going to work,” former CNN anchor Jim Acosta said. “They will start to fire anchors and certain folks to send a message, and the rest will either have to fall in line or leave. This was a colossal mistake.”One concerned CBS News staffer said that it “sounds like utter garbage”.“I’m happy to hear more about this, but how a board works day to day is tough to wrap my head around,” said a CNN producer who was not authorized to comment.Jessica J González, the co-chief executive of the advocacy organization Free Press, expressed doubts about the effectiveness of an oversight board.“As we learned from the failed and widely panned Facebook oversight board, a fake bipartisan oversight committee won’t save CNN,” she said in a statement on Monday. “We have all the evidence we need from the Ellisons’ destruction of CBS about what they do to warp journalism at Donald Trump’s request.”Frank Sesno, a former CNN Washington bureau chief who now teaches journalism at George Washington University, said the effectiveness of the oversight board will depend entirely on how it works.“I completely welcome an advisory group composed of professional journalists who can provide insight, feedback, critique and balance,” he wrote in an email. “It needs to consist of people who are committed for professional fact-based journalism and who understand the pressures and the complexities of the current media environment.”Connecticut’s attorney general, William Tong, who was part of the lawsuit coalition, said in a statement that his state “wanted and demanded full divestiture of CNN and CBS News”.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Around 2-3 times a daySign up toBreaking News USGet the most important news as it breaksEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“We wanted to save ethical and independent journalism and news,” he added. “We fought aggressively for that remedy. I am deeply disappointed that we could not do more.” Still, he said the board “will meaningfully help protect editorial independence for both news organizations, and it will be enforceable under the consent decree”.A similar board – of five purportedly independent individuals – was put in place when Rupert Murdoch acquired Wall Street Journal parent company Dow Jones in 2007, after concerns were raised about whether the conservative media baron would interfere with the news pages. It was “meant to prevent Murdoch from meddling in the Journal’s newsroom and maintain its editorial independence”,according to a news reportat the time, thoughsome concerns were raisedabout the independence of some of the board members.Last summer, Skydance Media agreed to appoint an independent ombudsman to secure the blessing of the Federal Communications Commission to merge with then CBS parent company Paramount Global.David Ellison has insisted that he will maintain editorial independence at CNN and has contended that the lawsuit filed by state attorneys general was primarily intended to block him from controlling the network. “I believe this fight is not really about market share,”he wrote in a guest essayin the New York Times last month. “If it were, it wouldn’t have been reviewed and approved by regulators reflecting 65 countries, including the United States and China, as well as the European Union. I believe a plainer worry sits beneath the briefs and the news releases: the news. The issue is whether I can be trusted as a steward of Warner’s CNN.“Great news organizations like CNN and CBS News are here to tell it straight down the middle,” he added. “That requires newsrooms that reflect the whole world, not one side of it. And it requires independence. Our journalists will continue to answer to the facts and to all the people they serve – not to any party or cause.”Still, Ellison’s commitments to independence have done little to quell the concerns of journalists at CNN and CBS News, particularly as the latter network has faced accusations of holding a partisan tilt under editor-in-chief Bari Weiss.In a statement about the settlement on Monday afternoon, Ellison made no mention of the editorial oversight board or any protections that will ensure CNN’s editorial independence.But in a nod to concerns about partisanship, the settlement agreement notes that “no more than two (2) editorial independence board members may be affiliated with the same political party”.Explore more on these topicsCNNCBSParamount+Warner BrosTV newsShareReuse this content

title: CNN, MS Now and Politico sue Trump after being blocked from White House | Donald Trump | The Guardian
description: Three news outlets filed lawsuit in attempt to regain access to the White House after having badges disabled
Author: Jeremy Barr
Headline: Three news outlets filed lawsuit in attempt to regain access to the White House after having badges disabled
Content: Donald Trump holds a news conference in the press briefing room of the White House on 6 April 2026.Photograph: Aaron Schwartz/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenDonald Trump holds a news conference in the press briefing room of the White House on 6 April 2026.Photograph: Aaron Schwartz/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty ImagesDonald TrumpCNN, MS Now and Politico sue Trump after being blocked from White HouseThree news outlets filed lawsuit in attempt to regain access to the White House after having badges disabledJeremy BarrMon 21 Sep 2026 10.42 EDTFirst published on Mon 21 Sep 2026 08.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIn what will be one of the largest battles yet between the press andDonald Trump’s administration, three news organizations – CNN, MS Now (formerly MSNBC) and Politico – that have beendenied accessto the White House have sued to regain their ability to enter the building, accusing the president of violating the US constitution.The suit was filed on Monday morning in the US district court forWashington DC.Journalists for the three news organizations were denied access to the White House and had their badges disabled on Saturday after the presidentdecreeda day earlier that they would lose their ability to enter the building because of his concerns about their coverage. The parties are seeking a temporary restraining order that would immediately lift the ban – and return access for the journalists – while the case plays out.“This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes,” the news organizations said in a statement, referring to the US constitutional amendment guaranteeing a free press.MS Now, CNN and Politico say reporters have been denied access to White HouseRead more“Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists’ credentials because it objected to our reporting. Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public’s right to independent journalism free from government interference.”In their lawsuit and request for a temporary restraining order, the parties argue that because the White House has granted access to journalists, those privileges cannot be rescinded based purely on viewpoint considerations. Case law heavily favors the plaintiffs, including past legal challenges that successfully returned the press badges of journalists Jim Acosta – then ofCNN– and Brian Karem, then of Playboy magazine, during Trump’s first presidency.“Defendants took these actions in express retaliation for Plaintiffs’ First Amendment-protected newsgathering and speech because they dislike that speech’s content and viewpoint, and for the express purpose of excluding journalists and news organizations with editorial viewpoints disfavored by theTrump administrationfrom the White House grounds,” lawyers for the news organization wrote in a motion, further alleging that the news organizations were unfairly deprived an opportunity to contest the ban as required by the fifth amendment of the US constitution.Laying out the stakes of the ban, the plaintiffs wrote that “they have been suffering serious irreparable harm”, adding: “They have already lost opportunities to perform their constitutionally protected newsgathering and reporting functions at the White House, impairing their ability to speak and publish as members of the press – and they lose more such opportunities every day that the ban remains in effect.”Trump announced the ban late last week in a post on Truth Social, writing that it was “a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS.” He added: “Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America.”Citing Trump’s own words, the news organizations wrote in their lawsuit that “this ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles.”While there was some uncertainty about whether Trump would follow through, it became clear that the ban was put into effect when journalists fromMS Nowand CNN attempted to access the building on Saturday morning but were told that their badges had been disabled and were taken.CNN was scheduled to serve as the television pooler on Monday. But the White House removed the organization from the five-member group that provides video of the president’s activities to the rest of the news media. CNN was scheduled to accompany Trump as he traveled to New York City for the United Nations general assembly.On Monday morning, subscribers of the White House television pool received a memo stating that there would be no pool coverage of the president. “This is to advise that, effective today, the TV pool will not be covering events designated as pool coverage of the President,” the memo reads. “This follows the White House’s position preventing CNN from fulfilling its assigned pool duties.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Around 2-3 times a daySign up toBreaking News USGet the most important news as it breaksEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIn a statement, the five television networks that make up the primary video pool covering the White House – Fox News, ABC News, CBS News, CNN and NBC News – said: “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”Trump bans CNN, MS Now and Politico from White HouseRead moreThe suspension of the television pool is an extraordinary escalation and a sign that Trump’s ban of CNN, MS Now and Politico crossed a line for the news organizations that cover the White House. (The Guardian has reached out to the White House for comment on the planned lawsuit.)Trump responded to news of the pending lawsuit in a post on Truth Social, writing: “The White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish. It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS, something that has grown like Cancer in our beloved United States of America. It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control. It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!”The Knight First Amendment Institute at Columbia University said on Monday that it would support the news organizations in their lawsuit.“We’re glad to see that these news organizations are suing,” Jameel Jaffer, the organization’s executive director, said in a statement. “The president’s decision to bar them from the White House for the content of their reporting is a flagrant violation of the First Amendment. It’s an attack both on press freedom and the public’s right to independent information about the government. We will support these news organizations in court.”Explore more on these topicsDonald TrumpTrump administrationUS politicsCNNMS NowUS press and publishingMedia lawnewsShareReuse this content

title: Starbucks baristas reel from surges in health insurance costs: ‘I’m considering a second job’ | Starbucks | The Guardian
description: Several workers say they’re opting to go without health coverage due to premium costs soaring this year
Author: Michael Sainato
Headline: Several workers say they’re opting to go without health coverage due to premium costs soaring this year
Content: A barista prepares a drink inside a Starbucks in New York on 24 February 2025.Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenA barista prepares a drink inside a Starbucks in New York on 24 February 2025.Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty ImagesStarbucksStarbucks baristas reel from surges in health insurance costs: ‘I’m considering a second job’Several workers say they’re opting to go without health coverage due to premium costs soaring this yearMichael SainatoMon 21 Sep 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 07.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleStarbucks workers say their health insurance premiums have soared this year, in some cases more than doubling, according to a recent survey conducted byStarbucksWorkers United.The survey of more than 130 Starbucks workers in both unionized and non-unionized stores, shared exclusively with the Guardian, found baristas are experiencing significant hikes in costs for their health insurance coverage starting 1 October.Some workers reported their premium costs per paycheck nearly doubling, even as they struggle to afford other basic necessities andare scheduled to work enough hours to be eligible for the benefits.The changes come as Starbucks Workers Unitedlauncheda boycott last month against the company demanding a union contract, what would be the first since stores started to unionize in December 2021. Since then,more than 700 Starbucks storeshave won union elections, with the union representing over 12,000 workers at the company.Several workers said they are opting to go without health insurance coverage due to the costs and the price hikes are forcing them to worry about whether they need to find an additional job.Kaye-Lani Story, who has been a barista in Edina, Minnesota, for nine years, said she took herself and her son to the doctor this month as their health insurance is set to lapse on 1 October. Her health insurance premiums were set to go from $130 a week to $170 a week, a 30% increase.“That is another $40 each week that I am not going to have in my income, if I choose to go with it, and that’s just not something that financially I can afford,” she said. “I have to drop my insurance because the company will not cover those costs when it’s clear that they’re definitely making enough.”In the past, Kaye-Lani was qualified to receive Minnesota’s state health insurance, but switched to the company’s health insurance plan when she made too much income to qualify.“I make too much to qualify for coverage through the state. I don’t make enough to keep my medical coverage through work, and so at this point, I just have to drop it completely,” she added. “During the winter, the heating bill goes up. During the summer, the electric bill goes up from the AC. There are just all these wavering things throughout the year that I have to pull from to be able to apply to expenses just to be able to keep a roof over my head and food on the table and whatnot, and then this happens, and it’s too much.”Cory Wagner has relied on Starbucks’s health insurance for five of the seven years he’s worked as a barista at Starbucks in Woods Cross, Utah, outside Salt Lake City.“This is the first year that [premiums] nearly doubled,” Wagner said. “My insurance rates are going up to a point where I am now having to consider getting a second job, potentially leaving the company.”Wagner relies on a heart medication to be able to work and noted the health insurance premium cost increases have made the out of pocket cost of his medication unaffordable. His health insurance premium cost went from $70 per biweekly paycheck to $122 per paycheck this year.“Now I’m kind of left at a point where I am choosing between paying for this medication and paying for my utility bills, paying for my groceries, paying for the gas that I need to get to work,” he said. “The company has the money to keep our insurance premiums the same. They have the money to help the partners that are actively making them money.”Starbucks Workers United has filed an unfair labor practice charge after the company did not respond to a request for information on health insurance coverage changes regarding what prompted the fee hikes and how Starbucks’s contribution to the healthcare costs were affected.A Starbucks spokesperson did not comment on the unfair labor practice chargebut said in an email “like employers across the country, we continue to face rising healthcare costs while remaining committed to providing quality, affordable healthcare coverage for full and part-time partners at Starbucks, beginning at just 20 hours per week.”Explore more on these topicsStarbucksUS unionsFood & drink industryUS work & careersHealth insurancenewsShareReuse this content

title: Converse apologizes and pulls ad that critics said evoked racist imagery | Advertising | The Guardian
description: Sneaker company removes social media ad after backlash from critics who said it resembled KKK imagery
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Sneaker company removes social media ad after backlash from critics who said it resembled KKK imagery
Content: The Converse world headquarters in the West End neighborhood of Boston on 28 December 2016.Photograph: Charles Krupa/APView image in fullscreenThe Converse world headquarters in the West End neighborhood of Boston on 28 December 2016.Photograph: Charles Krupa/APAdvertisingConverse apologizes and pulls ad that critics said evoked racist imagerySneaker company removes social media ad after backlash from critics who said it resembled KKK imageryAssociated PressMon 21 Sep 2026 08.03 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 09.51 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe sneaker company Converse has removed a social media ad that sparked outrage among critics who viewed it as evoking the Ku Klux Klan and lynching.The Instagram ad photo showedK-popsinger Karina wearing a skirt and holding a pair of Chuck 70 X sneakers. Critics lashed out online, saying that a white triangular image created by lighting on the skirt resembled aKKKhood – and that the way she held the sneakers made them look like the dangling feet of a lynching victim.Converse, owned byNike, issued a statement apologizing and saying it removed the ad.Target apologizes for ‘offensive’ Halloween costume after backlashRead more“We’re sorry,” said the statement, first released on Friday. “We understand why this image is deeply upsetting and recognize that we got this wrong. We removed it from our channels and are working to remove it everywhere it appeared. This should not have happened and we will do better.”Converse, based in Boston, declined on Sunday to answer questions seeking additional information, including how the company screens ads before they are posted and how the ad was approved.Karina and her management company, SM Entertainment Group, did not immediately respond to messages through their Instagram accounts.Retailers and top fashion brands have issued a string of apologies over the years for products criticized as being racially insensitive.In August, retailer Target pulled a children’s Halloween costume from its shelves after widespread social media backlash, apologizing for selling a garment that critics said evoked racist minstrel caricatures.The Converse photo sparked swift criticism, including calls for staff involved in the ad to be fired and for a boycott of the company. In a slew of comments on social media, posters questioned how the ad could have cleared the company’s advertising vetting process. Other commenters defended Converse, saying they didn’t believe it was intentional.Lee Merritt, a Texas-based civil rights attorney, posted on Instagram that Converse’s apology “doesn’t undo what got past legal, marketing and leadership at every step”.“We keep having this conversation because corporations keep failing the same test,” he wrote. “Do better means catching this before it airs – not after we’re offended.”Converse, founded in Malden, Massachusetts, in 1908, makes the Chuck Taylor All Star sneaker. It was first released in 1917 as a non-skid basketball shoe, adding the signature of Taylor – a basketball player who promoted the sneaker – in 1934, according to the company’s website.Explore more on these topicsAdvertisingNikeRaceSocial mediaMarketing & PRnewsShareReuse this content

title: Google fined more than €400m by Irish regulator over its use of location data | Google | The Guardian
description: Watchdog says users may have been unaware their information was used to target adverts or infer their interests
Author: Lisa O’Carroll
Headline: Watchdog says users may have been unaware their information was used to target adverts or infer their interests
Content: The DPC found that Google users could have been unaware of how their data was being used.Photograph: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe DPC found that Google users could have been unaware of how their data was being used.Photograph: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg/Getty ImagesGoogleGoogle fined more than €400m by Irish regulator over its use of location dataWatchdog says users may have been unaware their information was used to target adverts or infer their interestsLisa O’CarrollMon 21 Sep 2026 06.57 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGoogle has been fined more than €400m (£345m) over the way it processed users’ location data, following claims that the tech giant had manipulated users into agreeing to be constantly tracked on their mobile phones.The fine, imposed by Ireland’s Data Protection Commission (DPC), comes after complaints from multiple European consumer organisations that Google was following every step users took.Location-related adverts are familiar to holidaymakers, but seven European consumer organisations hadcomplained that undue use of location data can also lead to a breach of privacy.The DPC inquiry was prompted byresearch by the Norwegian consumer agency in 2018which suggested location data could reveal details such as religious beliefs (by tracking places of worship), political leanings (for example knowing a user has gone to demonstrations), health conditions (if a user has gone to hospital) and sexual orientation (if they have gone to certain bars).The DPC launched its inquiry six years ago and set out to find out whether Google had a valid legal basis for its use of location data.It found that Google users could have been unaware that their location was being used to influence them with adverts or to gather details about their health and interests.“Location data is a type of personal data which is processed by way of location tracking, and includes data collected or processed by Google, which by itself or in conjunction with other information an individual’s location can be inferred,” said Graham Doyle, a deputy commissioner at the DPC.“Location data can bring both benefits and harms to individuals.“It can greatly enhance the utility of online services, but it can also reveal a significant amount of information about an individual, including information that is inherently private,” Doyle added.Responding to the DPC’s ruling, a Google spokeperson said: “This case centres around historical policies that have since been updated. From 2019 onwards, we’ve significantly evolved our practices and launched robust tools that make managing location data simple.”The European Consumer Organisation (BEUC) based its complaint on research by the Forbrukerrådet, the Norwegian consumer agency, whichclaimed Google used “various tricks”to ensure location history and web and app activity were enabled.“Today marks an important milestone in the effort to protect our rights online. People must be able to understand what they are agreeing to without being deceived or manipulated into making choices they otherwise would never have made,” says Finn Myrstad, director of digital policy at the Norwegian Consumer Council.BEUC said that geolocation data was “one of the most invasive forms of consumer surveillance”.Agustín Reyna, director general of BEUC, welcomed the ruling but said “the time needed to come to this conclusion is disproportionate with the seriousness of the infringement” arguing “late enforcement can be as harmful as no enforcement at all”.The DPC inquiry looked at “web and app activity”, “location history” and “location accuracy” between 25 May 2018 and 4 February 2020.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionImposing a fine of €403m, the DPC ordered Google to bring its processing into compliance with the EU’s general data protection regulation (GDPR) within six months.It is the fourth-largest fine imposed by the Irish regulator, which has EU-wide responsibility for all the US tech giants with EU headquarters in Ireland.It has previously fined Meta €1.2bn, TikTok €530m and Instagram (also Meta owned) €405m.Doyle said: “The GDPR provides a high level of protection of personal data throughout the EEA, and requires that the processing of personal data must be carried out in a lawful, fair and transparent manner.AI slowdown calls justified but collapse of bubble may be more immediate threat | Heather StewartRead more“As a result of Google’s failures in this regard, individuals could have been unaware that their location was being used to, for example, influence them with ads or to infer their interests, and could lose control over their personal data.“The retention of users’ location data for longer than necessary aggravated this loss of control,” added Doyle.There are three other ongoing statutory large-scale inquiries open that concern Google, all of which are at an advanced stage.Explore more on these topicsGoogleEuropean UnionSmartphonesAlphabetMobile phonesEuropenewsShareReuse this content

title: Ten lessons from Jakob Ingebrigtsen, one of the world’s most beguiling athletes | Athletics | The Guardian
description: Jakob Ingebrigtsen is meticulous in his training regime – ‘if there’s anything that’s out of my control, then I’ve not done my job properly’
Author: Sean Ingle
Headline: Jakob Ingebrigtsen is meticulous in his training regime – ‘if there’s anything that’s out of my control, then I’ve not done my job properly’
Content: Jakob Ingebrigtsen loves running on his treadmill at home – ‘I put it on a certain speed, at a certain incline, and it’s always the same.’Photograph: Marie von Krogh/The GuardianView image in fullscreenJakob Ingebrigtsen loves running on his treadmill at home – ‘I put it on a certain speed, at a certain incline, and it’s always the same.’Photograph: Marie von Krogh/The GuardianAthleticsTen lessons from Jakob Ingebrigtsen, one of the world’s most beguiling athletesSean IngleNorwegian is meticulous in his training regime – ‘if there’s anything that’s out of my control, then I’ve not done my job properly’Mon 21 Sep 2026 15.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTShareOn a snowy Norwegian morning in January, Jakob Ingebrigtsen was on his treadmill, shooting the breeze about his running philosophy before our more formal interview. I should write something on this, I told him. Sure, came the reply.In recent weeks, the 26‑year‑old has added to his legacy witha European 5,000m gold, theWorld Ultimate 5,000m titleand a world road silver medal despite achilles surgery in February and a flu that lingered through May and June. So now seems as good a time as any.Some of Ingebrigtsen’s opinions were a little hardcore. Others reiterated basic truths. But whether you are a runner or not, there are certainly some life lessons from one of the most beguiling athletes around.At home with Jakob Ingebrigtsen: ‘I’ve fed my obsession my whole life’Read more1) To be the best it helps to be a control freakIngebrigtsen runs a lot, around 175-180km in a typical week. Apart from his family, that is his sole focus. “I prioritise the absolute crucial,” he says. “That is to wake up, to eat, to train.” It is, he concedes, not a life most would enjoy. “A lot of people could never be in my shoes, having my responsibility. They just wouldn’t handle it. But that’s how I want to be. If there’s anything that’s out of my control, then I’ve not done my job properly.”2) No days off“If you have a day off, you lose 20-25km of running,” he says. Counterintuitively, perhaps, he believes the risk of injury goes up too and tries to run even when he is moderately poorly.“Having one week off if you are sick, injured or travelling, or even just doing easier training, that’s probably the worst thing you can do in terms of risk of injury. Because you are taking your body out of a consistent load. When you get back again, you will have sore legs because your body is not adapted to that load and when you compensate, or just change symmetry a little bit, that’s when something snaps.”3) Consistency is kingIngebrigtsen runs twice a day, in the morning and afternoon, with hills on a Saturday and a longish run of 20km on a Sunday. He supplements this with drills, mobility and core work on Monday and Wednesday and weights every Friday and Sunday. He does this week after week after week unless he is injured. Consistency, and gradually increasing load, is a lesson he says amateur runners should apply.4) Be prepared to work very hardIngebrigtsen is famous for his double threshold runs on Tuesday and Thursdays – two runs each day that aim for the sweet spot between hard, but not brutal, fatigue, but sustainable. A morning session, for instance, might involve 5x6 minutes effort with a one‑minute jog for recovery between repetitions. In the afternoon it could be 25 times around a 400m track at 5km-10km pace with 30 seconds recovery.Ingebrigtsen says that while he runs more miles than his 1500m competitors, “the biggest difference is how often we train and the size of our sessions – we very rarely do more than 10km-12km of quality in one session”. He adds: “With having more sessions you can spread the volume out a lot more without having spikes and peaks in load.”5) No slacking even on Christmas Day“Last year, I ran twice and did 22k. I think that counts as an easy day,” he says, although he had to watch for digestion problems. “Christmas dinner in Norway is very rich in fat because we have pork ribs. I just had to be a little bit careful with the amount because we have different sausages, sheep and meat cakes too.”6) The treadmill is your friend,whatever time of year“I’ve always used treadmills, not only because of the conditions in Norway, but also to control a lot of the variables,” he says. “I put it on a certain speed, at a certain incline, and it’s always the same. It doesn’t matter if the wind is from the north or if it’s raining or cold.” He also does a morning threshold session on his treadmill, even in the height of summer, with punk and rock bands Green Day, Blink-182 and Black Sabbath topping his playlist.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenJakob Ingebrigtsen wins the 5,000m final at the Ultimate Championships in Budapest.Photograph: Xinhua/Shutterstock7) Fast shoes help with recovery tooIngebrigtsen wears speedy and bouncy shoes for most of his running, with the Nike Zoom Fly 6 among his favourites. “You can decrease the load and impact by the amount of cushioning that’s now available in shoes,” he says. “So if I can get out of my Monday to Sunday programme 95% fatigued, that is enabling me to do the same the next week with the same amount of quality … just with 5% extra intensity.”8) Training in mud is a waste of timeIngebrigtsen sneers at the old-school approach of lots of running on trails and cross-country. “It is pointless. Training in mud or grass is not something I believe in. Let’s say I was going into a field and all of a sudden I’m doing 1k reps in mud and stones. Think about the extra risk that I’m taking, not only in terms of load and training but also tripping and snapping my ankle? Why would I risk it?”9) Always question what coaches can teach youPerhaps this is explained by Ingebrigtsen’s relationship with his father and former coach Gjert, whohe ended up facing in court in 2025. But he is adamant that discussing everything with his brothers Henrik and Filip is better than a top-down approach.“With a lot of coaches, it’s more like a priest. You can get really attached to them and it’s almost dangerous in the way it takes away responsibility from the athlete. If you have an ex-professional runner as a coach, it is always going to be ‘I did this, I did that, this is what worked for me, this is something new and revolutionary’. I don’t believe in it.”10) You always have to keep yourself accountableSome truths are universal when it comes to running and life. “You have to take responsibility for yourself,” he says. “Each individual and every athlete needs to build their own toolbox regarding their qualities and maybe lack of qualities. Responsibility, I think that’s the key word. And accountability.”Explore more on these topicsAthleticsRunningTraining programmesDistance runningcommentShareReuse this content

title: Justin Herbert has been the quarterback of tomorrow his entire NFL career. Whose fault is that? | NFL | The Guardian
description: The Chargers star is huge, can run and has a golden right arm. But he has never quite reached the heights many expected for him
Author: Alex Kirshner
Headline: The Chargers star is huge, can run and has a golden right arm. But he has never quite reached the heights many expected for him
Content: Justin Herbert was the sixth overall pick in the 2020 draft.Photograph: Brooke Sutton/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJustin Herbert was the sixth overall pick in the 2020 draft.Photograph: Brooke Sutton/Getty ImagesNFLJustin Herbert has been the quarterback of tomorrow his entire NFL career. Whose fault is that?The Chargers star is huge, can run and has a golden right arm. But he has never quite reached the heights many expected for himAlex KirshnerMon 21 Sep 2026 03.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 12.26 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJustin Herbert is one of the most promising quarterbacks in theNFL. In fact, Justin Herbert has forever been one of the most promising quarterbacks in the NFL. That adjective, “promising”, continued to be load-bearing on Sunday, as Herbert and his Chargers turned in an underwhelming performance in a 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. Los Angeles are now 0-2 on the year, with those losses coming to the team who picked No 1 in this year’s draft and a moribund Arizona who picked No 3. Stockholders in Herbert’s growth were taking a beating in after-hours trading. But, as ever, there’s plenty of reason to debate whether Herbert underachieved or whether his team let him down.Herbert is 6ft 6in, can run, has a golden right arm and iscapable of making astonishing throws. NFL decision-makers view him as roughly the sixth-best QB in the leaguebut also say things like, “He should have more accolades at this point.” Certainly, he should have more wins this season, but on Sunday the 28-year-old found himself outdueled by one of the league’s senior citizens in Vegas quarterback Kirk Cousins, 10 years his senior. Herbert completed 15 of 27 passes for a touchdown and two interceptions, and he also took three sacks. Cousins threw a pick and took two sacks but was much more efficient from down to down (8.7 yards per attempt to Herbert’s 7.1). In 13 possessions, Los Angeles put together two long touchdown drives and otherwise didn’t march more than 30 yards in a series.NFL roundup: Bears QB Caleb Williams carted off in loss to Vikings; Saints stun RavensRead moreHow much of this is Herbert’s fault, though? It’s an eternal question, and one that came up after the Chargers’ playoff wildcard loss to the Patriots last season. In that game, Herbert played miserably but arguably had no chancenotto be terrible, because the New England defenders were in his face all evening. In almost any Herbert loss, one caneasilyfind examples of his teammates letting him down. Sunday was another good example. Herbert wasn’t terrific by any means, and given his billing, he’d ideally be able to get over failures by his teammates. But there’s not much the QB can do when tight end David Njoku bobbles a catch onan ever-so-slightly underthrown ball and turns it into an interception. Or when an under-pressure Herbert throws a ball that either of two receivers could catch without a problem, but one cuts off the other and drops it. Then there’s the injury luck – not so much to Herbert, who has generally been durable while playing through a number of injuries – but to those around him. Every year, a key member of his line or receiving corps seems to go down with a season-ending injury, leaving him exposed or without a weapon to deploy against opposing defenses. There are also question marks over the coaches who have overseen his career. Jim Harbaugh came to the Chargers with high expectations, but has yet to win a playoff game with the team, while Mike McDaniel, the team’s new offensive coordinator, has a reputation as a schematic whiz, but the offense has sputtered.Herbert, of course, must shoulder some of the blame himself. The Chargers have not done a good job of protecting him, but the very best quarterbacks find a way to win even when the pocket collapses. He is also 0-3 in the playoffs – a small sample size, but it still raises question marks about how he performs against the very best teams. Unfortunately, this season there have been question marks against very average teams too.The blame game will be in vogue this week. A team we expected to contend with the Chiefs and Broncos for the AFC West have already dug themselves a substantial hole, and they’ve done it while using up one of the easiest stretches of schedule that any team will face all year. The Chargers are the only 0-2 team in the division and one of just five in the AFC. To recover, they’ll need Herbert to be Superman. He has that gear, but consistency remains elusive, and the team’s margin for error is now awfully thin.MVP of the weekView image in fullscreenBrock Purdy has led his team to a 2-0 start to the season.Photograph: Kelley L Cox/APBrock Purdy, QB, San Francisco 49ers.According to ESPN’s QBR ratings, Purdy hadone of the 10 best games by a quarterbacksince the rankings began in 2006. (In case you’re wondering, the bestwas by Carson Palmer in 2009.) Admittedly, Purdy was playing against the Dolphins on Sunday but hewassuperb: he completed 20 of his 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns. He was also his team’s leading rusher with 30 yards and a touchdown on three carries. This came after another three-touchdown performance in the season opener against the No Sleep Till Melbourne Los Angeles Rams. Most of us expected the Niners to settle for a wildcard place out of the stacked NFC West this season but at this rate they could take the division.Stat of the week56.How many fewer points the Bears scored in their loss to the Vikings on Sunday, compared with their 59-37 romp over Carolina in Week 1. Chicago entered the week on as much of a spiritual high as the franchise has enjoyed in decades but ended it in a much more concerning place. Minnesota defensive coordinator Brian Flores had Caleb Williams and the offense in a blender all afternoon, and then things got considerably worse in the fourth quarter. That’s when Williams injured his hamstring, seriously enough that he wasn’t putting weight on his right leg as he walked off the field. (Reporters did see himwalking under his own poweras he left the locker room later.) Bears head coach Ben Johnson said he was “happy it’s nothing with the knee”, ruling out a torn ACL, and that the team would learn more on Monday.Video of the weekAllow content provided by a third party?This article includes content hosted onembed.bsky.app. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as the provider may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continueThe Steelers’ dreadful offense painted their masterpiece on a third-and-7 at the Patriots’ 22-yard line, in a game that CBS subject millions to as its national game of the week with Jim Nantz and JJ Watt in the booth. Trailing 10-0 in the second quarter, Aaron Rodgers took a shotgun snap and quickly found himself in a New England situation, as his blockers let pass rushers converge from both his left and right. What followed was a circus. Both teams booted the ball on the ground for a solid seven seconds. The catastrophe came to a humorous end when the Steelers’ left tackle, 317-pounder Troy Fautanu, fell on the ball for a loss of 36 yards that pushed Pittsburgh out of field-goal range. The Patriots went on to win 20-3. The Steelers’ offense looks even worse this year under 42-year-old Rodgers and his once-and-present head coach, the supposed offensive thinker Mike McCarthy.Elsewhere around the leagueWilliams wasn’t the only top-two pick from the 2024 draft to get hurt. Commanders QB Jayden Daniels did not make it through his team’s 37-20 loss at the Cowboys. Particularly upsetting was the location of his injury: the same left elbow that Daniels dislocated last season. An offensive lineman stepped on Daniels’s foot during an under-center exchange, and he appeared to hurt the elbow while trying to break his fall to the turf. A replay of Daniels’s elbow bending in the wrong direction prompted a relatable exclamation of “oh shit” from Tom Brady, watching from the Fox booth. Daniels throws with his right arm (ie: not the one injured here), but that’s only of mild comfort to the Commanders. Washington head coach Dan Quinnsaid after the gamethat Daniels had indeed dislocated his elbow again, although no bones were broken. The quarterback is expected to return at some point this season.View image in fullscreenJayden Daniels falls to the ground after his injury on Sunday.Photograph: Amanda Mccoy/TNS/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockSpare a thought for the players in the Eagles’ win over the Titans in Nashville. Fox reported that the turf (not the air) temperature reached 157F (69.4C) andsome players’ cleats even melted. “It was hot as shit, everybody was as hot as shit,”Eagleshead coach Nick Sirianni said after his team’s 24-20 win. “I didn’t play a snap and I had to get an IV.”View image in fullscreenDeVonta Smith makes a catch to score for the Eagles.Photograph: John Amis/APThe Browns beat the Buccaneers behind an unusually competent effort from their pitiful quarterback, Deshaun Watson. The QB on the losing end was Baker Mayfield, whom the Browns chased off after 2021 so that they could sign Watson to the worst contract in football history. Watson has spent his Browns career either injured, ineffective or suspended after the league looked into allegations of serial sexual misconduct. Watson’s 24-of-30 effort for 238 yards and two touchdowns doesn’t absolve him, or the Browns, of anything, but it does save the franchise a bit of short-term embarrassment that would have come with Mayfield beating them.The Panthers enjoyed one of the most dominant wins of the young season, a 34-3 destruction of a Falcons team who again started third-string QB Cooper Rush (and also played training camp darling Jack Strand, an undrafted rookie from Division II Minnesota State-Moorhead). The story here was about a QB with a more robust pedigree: Bryce Young, whose career looks like it may amount to something after all. The 2023 No 1 pick came on strong in the last few months of last season and played well. Young averaged eight yards per throw while avoiding interceptions. Even better, Young’s sharpest connection was with 2025 first-round wideout Tetairoa McMillan, who torched Atlanta corner AJ Terrell Jr for a 26-yard completion in the first three minutes and went on to a 101-yard day. Young remains a work in progress – his third-down performance left much to be desired, and he took two sacks – but seeing that progress doesn’t require a squint. Most of the best performances of Young’s career have come between last November and now.The Chiefs have enjoyed many charmed moments in the Andy Reid-Patrick Mahomes era. They almost pulled off their greatest trick yet on Sunday Night Football against the Colts. Then they didn’t, yet they won anyway. After kicking a field goal to take the lead on the first possession of overtime, the Chiefs turned the game over to their defense. A stop would win the game, a field goal would extend it, and a touchdown would hand it to the Colts. Daniel Jones connected on a 48-yard bomb to journeyman wideout Laquon Treadwell, who went to the ground, got up, ran in a circle for a moment and then seemingly fumbled away the game to the Chiefs. But video review found that Treadwell had possessed the ball before he was touched on his way to the ground, meaning the sequence that led to his fumble never really happened. Granted a reprieve, Indianapolis played ultra-conservatively and knotted things at 30-30 on a field goal. Surprisingly to no one but Colts coach Shane Steichen, Patrick Mahomes retook possession and marched the Chiefs to a winning field goal by Harrison Butker. Some guys have all the luck, even in the rare instances when they don’t. The Colts have now lost nine in a row.Explore more on these topicsNFLLos Angeles ChargersUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Bears say Caleb Williams is week-to-week with hamstring injury and will ‘miss some time’ | Chicago Bears | The Guardian
description: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams’s hamstring injury is going to be a ‘week-to-week thing’, Chicago coach Ben Johnson said Monday
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams’s hamstring injury is going to be a ‘week-to-week thing’, Chicago coach Ben Johnson said Monday
Content: Caleb Williams gives the thumbs up as he is carted off the field on Sunday.Photograph: Mark Black/UPI/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenCaleb Williams gives the thumbs up as he is carted off the field on Sunday.Photograph: Mark Black/UPI/ShutterstockChicago BearsBears say Caleb Williams is week-to-week with hamstring injury and will ‘miss some time’Quarterback sustained injury in loss on SundayTyson Bagent lined up to replace WilliamsReutersMon 21 Sep 2026 14.05 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 14.54 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBears quarterbackCaleb Williams’s hamstring injuryis going to be a “week-to-week thing,” Chicago coach Ben Johnson said Monday in a ⁠radio interview on ESPN 1000.Johnson did not put a definitive timeline on Williams’s recovery.“He’s going to miss some time. I haven’t met with the trainers ⁠yet but will have the full lowdown,” Johnson said. “He does tend to recover from these things quickly.”‘I needed an IV’: shoes melt as turf temperature reaches 157F in Eagles-Titans gameRead moreWilliams was hurt when attempting to reach the end zone ⁠with a fourth-quarter scramble on the wet turf at Soldier Field. He awkwardly tumbled to the ​turf on his knees and rolled over a ‌couple times in pain ‌before the Bears’ medical staff attended to him.The initial reporting on Sunday said that Williams sustained a Grade 1 hamstring strain.The Ringer reportedthat Williams could play next week against the Eagles, although Johnson’s statement suggests that scenario is doubtful.The 24-year-old has made 36 consecutive starts since the Bears drafted him No 1 overall in 2024. He has completed 65.5% of ‌his passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception this season for Chicago, who are 1-1 this season.If Williams is unable to go next Monday against the Eagles, it would ​mark the first time Johnson has been forced to start a backup quarterback as an offensive play caller. Jared Goff started all 51 games for the Lions from 2022-24, when Johnson was Detroit’s offensive coordinator.Chicago backup Tyson Bagent completed 5 of 9 passes for 54 yards in relief on Sunday. He has ⁠thrown for 971 yards, three TDs and six interceptions in 13 games (four starts) ​over the last four seasons. ​All four of his starts ​came as a rookie in 2023 for Chicago.If Bagent is called upon ​to start, Johnson ‌said he has ​confidence in the quarterback.“He’s wired ​the right way. Having a full week of preparation can make all the difference in performance,” Johnson said of Bagent. “I said at the combine, we view him as one of the top 32 [quarterback in the NFL]. The way he approaches it, his teammates are going to fight their tails off for him.”Explore more on these topicsChicago BearsNFLUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘I needed an IV’: shoes melt as turf temperature reaches 157F in Eagles-Titans game | NFL | The Guardian
description: The Tennessee Titans were happy to get off the field on Sunday, and not just because they lost their second game of the season
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: The Tennessee Titans were happy to get off the field on Sunday, and not just because they lost their second game of the season
Content: Tennessee’s Jacob Martin tries to stay cool in the heat.Photograph: George Walker IV/APView image in fullscreenTennessee’s Jacob Martin tries to stay cool in the heat.Photograph: George Walker IV/APNFL‘I needed an IV’: shoes melt as turf temperature reaches 157F in Eagles-Titans gameEagles coach says game was ‘hot as shit’Cam Jurgens had to replace cleats several timesGuardian sportMon 21 Sep 2026 00.33 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 09.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Tennessee Titans were happy to get off the field on Sunday, and not just because theylost their second game in a row.Amid sweltering conditions in Nashville, the temperature on the artificial turf at Nissan Stadium reached 157F (69.4C), according to the Fox broadcast.My son’s death during a college football workout was preventable. Lessons must be learnedRead more“It was hot as shit, everybody was as hot as shit,”Philadelphia Eagleshead coach Nick Sirianni said after his team’s 24-20 win. “I didn’t play a snap and I had to get an IV. I … appreciate how much the players fought through because it wasn’t easy.”Allow content provided by a third party?This article includes content hosted onembed.bsky.app. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as the provider may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continueNashville was under a heat warning for Sunday’s game, which kicked off at noon local time. The air temperature was 95F (35C) with a heat index of 105F (40.5C). However, inside the bowl of the stadium the surface of the artificial turf was much hotter.Eagles offensive lineman Jordan Mailata said the temperatures were another reason for the players’ union to push for a ban on artificial turf.“I’ve never thought about how hot a stadium can be if it’s turf. [The heat] just sits there and bounces up into you,” Mailata said. “[The union] have got to bring it up. This is why we want all grass fields, to create a standard of play in the league where we’re not putting players in dangerous positions if we don’t have to.”The Fox broadcast showed water being poured on players’ shoes to keep them cool, and Mailata’s teammate Cam Jurgens said he had to replace his cleats several times because they melted.“Half-time was like a Nascar pit crew helping me get ready for the second half,” Jurgens said. “That turf was just radiating.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionConditions were also tough last week in Tennessee’s season opener against the New York Jets. In that game, Titans safety Amani Hooker said the midsole on one of his shoes “melted completely off”.ESPN reportedthat some players and staff had questioned why the league scheduled an afternoon kickoff in September in a city known for its hot and humid conditions. There has been attention in recent years on college playerswho have diedwhile training in high temperatures, and former Eagles safety Reed Blankenship had to leave a game in 2024 with a heat-related illness.Explore more on these topicsNFLTennessee TitansPhiladelphia EaglesUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Infantino proposes an ‘independent external review’ of Fifa governance | Fifa | The Guardian
description: The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has agreed to commission an independent governance review, in the wake of the World Cup sale debacle
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has agreed to commission an independent governance review, in the wake of the World Cup sale debacle
Content: Gianni Infantino acknowledged to members that Fifa’s handling of a now-abandoned investment plan has caused concern.Photograph: Jarek Praszkiewicz/EPAView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino acknowledged to members that Fifa’s handling of a now-abandoned investment plan has caused concern.Photograph: Jarek Praszkiewicz/EPAFifaInfantino proposes an ‘independent external review’ of Fifa governancePresident writes to council and member nationsInfantino says he is ‘fully committed to leading Fifa’Matt HughesMon 21 Sep 2026 17.05 EDTFirst published on Mon 21 Sep 2026 16.15 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Fifa president,Gianni Infantino, has agreed to commission an independent governance review after coming under mounting pressure to do so in the wake of the World Cup sale debacle.The Guardian revealed last month that several members of the Fifa council had been lobbying for an external review of both the proposed Fifa Forward Enterprise sell-off and the Folarin Balogun controversy – with the Football Association chair, Debbie Hewitt, increasing the pressure last week by writing to Infantinodemanding the release of all documents relating to both issues.Uefa and Concacaf ask Gianni Infantino to give Fifa’s billions to its member associationsRead moreInfantino opted not to engage with the disgruntled members of the council, but in a letter sent to all 211 of Fifa’s member associations he has indicated his willingness to submit to external scrutiny for the first time.In addition, Infantino also invited proposals to review Fifa’s internal decision-making processes, which he said would be discussed at the next Fifa council meeting in Zurich on 15 October.“First, I will ask the council whether it wishes to commission an independent external review of Fifa’s current governance framework for major strategic initiatives and recommend potential improvements,” Infantino wrote.“Second, I will propose that the council establish a direct, structured and time-limited consultation with confederations, member associations and relevant stakeholders on how Fifa’s decision-making can be further strengthened.“The consultation would invite specific proposals on earlier institutional involvement, the respective roles of the president, the bureau, the council and the congress, and practical ways to strengthen transparency, participation and accountability in major strategic initiatives.”The Fifa Council, which comprises 28 representatives of the six confederations, eight vice-presidents and Infantino, is certain to approve the commissioning of an external review, although its terms of reference will be crucial in determining whether the world governing body is open to significant change or whether this represents the latest attempt by Infantino to shore up his power base before the presidential election in March next year.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAll the presidents’ meddling: the Balogun scandal shows how Fifa can break football | Barney RonayRead moreIn his letter to the member associations, Infantino does not commit to reviewing FFE and Balogun specifically, however, so has stopped short of bowing to Hewitt’s demands.Infantino is also under pressure to release money from Fifa’s $6bn (£4.5bn) cash reserves to its members, with the presidents of Uefa, and north and central American confederation Concacaf, Aleksander Ceferin and Victor Montagliani last week making a formal request for a payout of at least $10m for each national association.The Asian Football Confederation president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, sent a similar letter on Monday with the issue of funding also to be on the agenda at the Fifa Council meeting next month.Explore more on these topicsFifaGianni InfantinoFootball title: Paper trail of protests: José Mourinho plays the hits in Madrid derby defeat | La Liga | The Guardian
description: Facing Diego Simeone 13 years on, José Mourinho brought a print-out and paranoia. Some things don’t change. Some people don’t change much, either
Author: Sid Lowe
Headline: Facing Diego Simeone 13 years on, José Mourinho brought a print-out and paranoia. Some things don’t change. Some people don’t change much, either
Content: José Mourinho holding up an A4 paper showing two moments he thought were red cards in the Madrid derby.Photograph: SkyJosé Mourinho holding up an A4 paper showing two moments he thought were red cards in the Madrid derby.Photograph: SkyLa LigaPaper trail of protests: José Mourinho plays the hits in Madrid derby defeatFacing Diego Simeone 13 years on, José Mourinho brought a print-out and paranoia. Some things don’t change. Some people don’t, eitherSid LoweMon 21 Sep 2026 11.13 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 11.40 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere were many questions to emerge from the Madrid derby, whichAtlético won 2-1in front of 70,514 very, very noisy people at the Metropolitano on Sunday afternoon, even if not the one José Mourinho was asking. Like: what year is this? Or: what was Dean Huijsen thinking? Why always Arda? And whatever happened to Vinícius Júnior? How come Koke isstillthe best? And how long before Giuliano Simeoneactuallybursts, hisatléticoinsides exploding across the pitch? Above all though, you were left wondering: where did Real Madrid’s manager get a printer from? And how did he get the bloody thing to work?You could still hear the singing outside when Mourinho turned up in the press room, laid down his glasses and sat. In his hand was a piece of paper. Thirteen years after his last derby, on the Santiago Bernabéu night whenMadrid lost the Copa del Rey finaland a13-yearunbeaten run against their neighbours, Diego Simeone had defeated him again. The stage was new –this stadium didn’t exist then– but his adversary was somehow still the same man, still dressed in black, and the scene was a bit like old times, a classic. Mourinho unfolded the paper and held it up. “We can save ourselves the bother of the press conference,” he said, “because the story is right here.”Printed on the back side of an Atlético info sheet were two screen grabs from the first half, one on top of the other. Someone had been sent to run off a copy, some footballing Natalie Harp or the manager himself coming back with a couple of gory, freeze-framed, full-colour closeups of tackles. The first showed Cuti Romero’s studs catching Jude Bellingham’s knee; the second showed Kang-in Lee on Fede Valverde’s ankle. Both should have been red, Mourinho insisted, and he was probably right, but neither was. It should have been nine against 11, he said; instead, it was 11 against 10 because early in the second half Huijsen dragged Giuliano Simeone down for the penalty that gave Atlético the lead and got him sent off. And that, Mourinho said, was that. End of story.View image in fullscreenReal Madrid’s Dean Huijsen was sent off after conceding a penalty to Atlético’s Giuliano Simeone during the derby.Photograph: Juan Carlos Lucas/Zuma Press Wire/ShutterstockAt which point he could have got up and gone, saved everyone the bother of the press conference like he promised, but no one wants that,least of all his president, and that’s the bit he does best so he carried on. Five questions he faced. Four of them were about the referee; so was the answer to the one that was not about the referee. And when he had finished, leaving the paper there for Diego Simeone to have a look at, most agreed:nowMourinho is back, and he’s playing the greatest hits, a hint of the nostalgia that had brought him “home” in the first place, a hint of the conspiratorial mindset too, echoes of him reading out13 “errors” made by the referee Clos Gómez16years earlier.Ghosts of 2023 quelled after Dortmund return to the Bundesliga summit | Andy BrassellRead moreThe “poor ref” – just 41, not an international, and named in advance rather than 24 hours before kick-off – couldn’t handle the pressure, which was “like the 1980s”, Mourinho claimed. The coach, who had already revived his famous “porqué” (why?) line after they lost at Betis, also ran through a list of decisions made by the referee in the VAR room, Daniel Trujillo Suárez – a man supposedly with history – which “make you laugh”. There was talk of “strange things” happening. He insisted he didn’twantto think ill of officials, didn’twantto say the league has been “set up” for others to win, didn’twantto think that these were anything other than honest mistakes –of course not. Hecongratulatedthe referees’ committee and vowed to fight for the title despite being six points behind already –ifthey let us. “I thought I would come back to find a different league to the one I left, but [at Madrid] they told me not and explained why not,” he said.What Mourinho didn’t say was anything really about the actual football, which might be because there wasn’t much football. The cards might have conditioned the game – of course they might – and he was entitled to insist on the reds, although you could debate Romero’s. But it was hard to avoid the feeling that Mourinho purposely missed a deeper point and revealed a deeper reality, that there could be no escaping the reality he sought to escape: that Madrid are just not very good. That too many questions were avoided and another could be asked:is that it? There was little evidence to back his brief claim that they played well in the first half and were set up to win it in the second – how? – and even if true, it pointed to something limited: wait, counter and it will come.With the players Madrid have, often it will, but Atlético were aware of that, planned for it; they were aware too of where the damage could be done, overloading Madrid’s left. Simeone’s side took more than twice as many shots and had two-thirds of the possession. They had done so cautiously, it is true, but they, not Madrid, had exercised control. Mourinho’s team had offered little before the potential reds, their first shot on target coming on 39 minutes and from 25 yards, and even less after the actual red, Atlético’s half unoccupied for most of the period except by a pigeon. With Guler withdrawn, their reaction didn’t exist. It’s not easy with 10 men, but there was barely a spark. Even the goal they did get in the 89th minute was an isolated moment and, for all the nerves at the Metropolitano, was followed by more chances for Atlético.Quick GuideLa Liga resultsShowEspanyol 1-3 Elche, Sevilla 1-3 Barcelona, Celta Vigo 5-0 Real Santander, Athletic Bilbao 0-0 Alavés, Osasuna 1-1 Rayo Vallecano, Valencia 2-3 Real Sociedad, Villarreal 3-1 Levante, Deportivo A Coruña 1-1 Real Betis, Atlético 2-1 Real Madrid, Getafe 1-0 MálagaWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.None of which would matter so much as a one-off, but these flaws were familiar. Madrid needed last-minute Carlos Espí goals tobeat Espanyoland Elcheand they’re still six points off the top already. It’s not even close to definitive just seven weeks in and Madrid’s rebuilding process has only just begun, but basic issues they have faced for the last two years remain unaddressed; Fabio Capello’s implausible2006-07 league title winis the only time Barcelona have ever had a lead that big at the top of the table and lost it. Hansi Flick’s team are flying; and right now you wouldn’t trust Madrid to take advantage even if they did slip up. Claude Makélélé summed them up as: “Nothing, nothing, nothing.” Which leaves only this: a print-out and paranoia, a campaign. Some things don’t change. Some people don’t change much, either.View image in fullscreenJonathan David (right) score the winner in a Madrid derby which Atlético dominated.Photograph: Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto/ShutterstockSome, though, do. The last time these two coaches met in a derby,Simeone’s son Giulianowas told he was too little to go to the final so he hung scarves around the living room and watched it from home with his brothers instead. It was late, it was a school night, and he was only 10. He is 23 now and these days he plays for them, a bundle of intensity going at it the way a fan would, and on the day these two “colleagues of war” – as Mourinho called them – met again 13 years later he decided the derby, forcing the penalty for the first and setting up the second. There is some footage somewhere of Giuliano as a ballboy racing up the touchline and leaping into his father’s arms, celebrating wildly whenAtlético scored against Madrid. A decade on, another derby day, and it happened again, only this time it was his dad sprinting up the line towards him.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionTalking points“We give him the ball, he scores the goals,” Fermín López said. Over and over and over again. Raphinha, who isfilling in at centre forward, has now scored 12 league goals in just seven games, plus two more in the Champions League. He is five ahead of anyone else already. On Saturday night he scored an outrageously good hat-trick, the movement every inch the No 9, the touch and finishing at ridiculous speed all his, as Barcelona beat Sevilla 3-1. Sevilla went a goal up and were as good as anyone against Flick’s side so far this season but in the end just couldn’t live with them, coach Luis García calling them “stratospheric”. That’s seven wins from seven (eight from eight in all competitions), and31goals already, the captain leading the way. And not just with the goals, but with everything, taking everyone on a wild intense ride with him. Raphinha says thatLamine Yamal should win the Ballon d’Orbut right now there’s no one quite like him anywhere. That said, Lamine Yamal wasabsurdat the Pizjuan.At the end of their 0-0 draw with Athletic, Alavés goalkeeper Antonio Sivera walked off saying: “At last, at last!” His record was, he said, “ridiculous” but now at last he had done it. A European champion at U21 level, he is 30 now, and he had just saved the first penalty of his entire career.“When I played football as a kid in Croatia, everyone wants to play in one of Europe’s top five leagues and on my list Spain was bottom, but in the end it seems like Osasuna and La Ligaismy place: God’s path is different to mine,”said Ante Budimiron Saturday, after a lovely chest-and-volley goal took him to 100 in Spain.Speaking of which, what a way to celebratethe 100th birthdayof your home.PosTeamPGDPts1Barcelona724212Atletico Madrid79163Real Betis72164Real Madrid710155Sevilla71136Alaves75117Deportivo A Coruna72108Real Sociedad7-4109Villarreal71810Athletic Bilbao61811Getafe7-3812Rayo Vallecano7-5813Osasuna7-7814Celta Vigo72715Espanyol70716Racing Santander7-10717Levante6-4518Elche7-6519Valencia7-9420Malaga7-93Explore more on these topicsLa LigaReal MadridJosé MourinhoDiego SimeoneRefereesEuropean club footballAtlético MadridfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: The last two seasons were grim for Spurs. This is as bad as it’s ever been | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Pre-season thoughts of European qualification are already beginning to look bafflingly optimistic for Roberto De Zerbi’s team
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: Pre-season thoughts of European qualification are already beginning to look bafflingly optimistic for Roberto De Zerbi’s team
Content: Andy Robertson, Roberto De Zerbi and James Maddison were left disappointed on Saturday after another Spurs defeat.Composite: Shutterstock, GettyView image in fullscreenAndy Robertson, Roberto De Zerbi and James Maddison were left disappointed on Saturday after another Spurs defeat.Composite: Shutterstock, GettySoccer with Jonathan WilsonPremier LeagueThe last two seasons were grim for Spurs. This is as bad as it’s ever beenPre-season thoughts of European qualification are already beginning to look bafflingly optimistic for Roberto De Zerbi’s teamSign up for our free newsletter hereJonathan WilsonMon 21 Sep 2026 11.20 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 18.34 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIn March, Tottenham, fearing possible relegation, spent big to bring in Roberto De Zerbi, who will probably never go into a negotiation with a stronger hand. There was obvious improvement and they stayed up on the final day of the season. Since then, Spurs have spent a net £175m ($234m) on improving the squad. The message seemed clear: the fiscal caution of the Daniel Levy era was over and this was a club willing to spend. Yet Spurs go into the first international breakbottom of the Premier League table.To an extent, the issue is confidence. On the opening weekend at Brentford, with a weird mishmash of a side, a team that was clearly undercooked, they were hammered 3-0 by much better-prepared opponents. That was not hugely surprising given how sensible Brentford’s transfer dealing had been and how early they had done it. More worrying was what happened the following week as Spurs, starting well before fading, lost 2-0 at home to Newcastle.Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s actionRead moreGoalless draws against Nottingham Forest and Everton seemed to have steadied the ship. Their biggest problem seemed to be a lack of confidence. They were tentative in possession, indecisive when chances did come. The two goals they managed in their3-2 defeat to Aston Villaon Saturday mean Spurs climbed above Coventry to second-bottom of the goal-scoring charts, but they are ninth for shots. That should be reason for frustration rather than panic; the goals will come eventually.But there are more concerning things to have come out of Saturday’s game. The lack of confidence in front of goal seems to have curdled into something worse, a more general mental degeneration. Again, they started well. The Villa keeper Zion Suzuki made a string of saves. And then just before half-time Villa scored a shambolic goal. Micky van de Ven was off the pitch receiving treatment. Andy Robertson, in preventing the ball running out for a corner, gifted possession to John McGinn. A cut-back, a scuffed shot and Johan Manzambi was unmarked in the six-yard box to score. It was a horrible goal to concede.The second goal they conceded was just as bad. A long punt not dealt with, Nicolas Jackson bringing the ball down, Van de Ven not getting tight enough, a shot that bounced in off Antonin Kinsky’s hand. The third Villa goal was whipped brilliantly into the top corner by Emi Buendía, but he had space to line it up before James Maddison, who had been marking João Gomes, got out to him. Perhaps Maddison could have been more aggressive, and the slight turn of his back as Buendía struck his shot is never a good sign, but this was at least as much a failure of structure.To an extent Spurs were unfortunate. Robertson might have cleared that ball for a throw-in, or at least got distance down the line, and Boubacar Kamara’s mishit cross could have gone anywhere. Jackson will not always be so deft in taking down a chest-high ball. Buendía, enormously technically gifted as he is, will not always pick out the top corner. But equally, each goal followed some sort of error: thePremier Leagueis full of high-class players who will take advantage of any slip.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWhy Tottenham are misfiring … and it’s not just down to the lack of goalsRead moreDe Zerbi spoke of Spurs being “too fragile”, by which he seemed to be talking both of their physicality and mentality. They have players returning from injury. Like so many clubs, they brought in players late. Preseasons have been curtailed, perhaps inadequate.Where the initial instinct was to be impressed by the numbers and the change of policy, doubts are now emerging about the nature of those summer signings. Is Sandro Tonali really worth £100m? Mateus Fernandes played for a relegated side. Jan Paul van Hecke wouldn’t be the first player to leave Brighton and find his level dip outside that precisely configured environment. Sávio and Omar Marmoush struggled to get into the team at Manchester City. Sávio’s finishing brought just two league goals in two seasons at City and the evidence of Saturday is that it has not improved.The sense had been that this season couldn’t be as bad as the last two for Spurs. There is no Europe to distract them. The injury crises couldn’t be as bad again. De Zerbi has proved his worth in the Premier League before. They have spent money. And yet this is as bad as it’s ever been. Once a club of Tottenham’s stature could have dismissed this as a blip, the kind of thing that would inevitably sort itself out as the season went on. After the last two seasons, nobody can be quite that confident again.It’s still implausible Spurs could be relegated, unlikely even that they’ll be in another fight, but those preseason thoughts of European qualification are already beginning to look bafflingly optimistic – and that will inevitably slow the rebuilding of the club.This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US.Subscribe for free here.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueSoccer with Jonathan WilsonTottenham HotspurnewslettersShareReuse this content
