title: Come back soon Premier League, the endlessly moreish mega-product | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Brighton have impressed in a goal-laden start to the season, in a league that remains a brutally strong attraction
Author: Barney Ronay
Headline: Brighton have impressed in a goal-laden start to the season, in a league that remains a brutally strong attraction
Content: Brighton outskilled and outmuscled Arsenal on their way to a 3-0 victory last weekend.Photograph: Daniel Weir/Sports Press Photo/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenBrighton outskilled and outmuscled Arsenal on their way to a 3-0 victory last weekend.Photograph: Daniel Weir/Sports Press Photo/ShutterstockPremier LeagueCome back soon Premier League, the endlessly moreish mega-productBrighton have impressed in a goal-laden start to the season, in a league that remains a brutally strong attractionBarney RonayMon 21 Sep 2026 16.30 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGet ready for the dopamine crash. And this one really is a proper autumn nosedive. The past 17 days up to and including Sunday’s cut-off gave us 30Premier Leaguegames and 79 goals. Which, if you take Spurs out of it – and this is fair because Spurs are now post‑goal, an entertainment concept unrelated to goals or even football itself – is really quite a lot.Are your pathways stimulated? Are the neural connectors flickering? Well get ready for cold turkey, for 19 blank days of shivers and shakes until the Premier League show resumes in October. Maybe it really is time to buy one of those powders off the internet.The last two seasons were grim for Spurs. This is as bad as it’s ever been | Jonathan WilsonRead moreThe international break will provide its own intrigue. There will be discussions about whether Thomas Tuchel is or isn’t responsible for the inherited cultural weaknesses of English football. There will be rage at Tuchel’s inability to coach the players to keep the ball as never before via his few short hours on the training pitch. And yet more rage at the real issues, basically the fact he continues to be German and looks like a scurvy-ridden Napoleonic naval commander powered solely by ship’s biscuits and morphine.This is unlikely to fill the hole. There will be an unavoidable “contrast effect”, the rush of adrenaline that only serves to deepen the low when it is gone. But there are also some familiar autumn rituals to help us through. One of these is the state‑of‑the‑nation Premier League address, pegged out around key questions such as “where are we?”, “what are we?” and “where is it all going?”. This time around these are relatively easy to answer.Five rounds into the Premier League season this is pretty much a cut-and-paste job. The big news: there is no big news. Events continue to happen at great volume. But in terms of teams, style, stars, energies and potential outcomes, not much has changed. Roll back one year and this was the broad situation. A powerful team with a bald, irascible manager had won all five games, but also looked defensively fragile. The team that would win the league was second. That team was also Arsenal.View image in fullscreenAre Tottenham doomed? Probably not. They have enough semi-interested players to retain a solid hold on 17th place.Photograph: News Images/NurPhoto/ShutterstockThe middle classes were the most interesting story, those functional, well-run teams beginning with B, an entity you might call Brightonmouth. Erling Haaland was scoring goals. Bruno Fernandes was generating hair‑tearing anguish, like a young Elvis, but based more around shithousery and risky attacking passes.As ever there are still some key questions doing the rounds, but luckily these can all be answered easily. Is Michael Carrick the man to take Manchester United to the next level? No. Is Michael Carrick the reasonUnited are not at that level, but in a state where they must now employ Michael Carrick? Also no.The reality for United is that there are no other levels. This is the level, a club that instead acts as a grand, angst-ridden but very accurate metaphor for modern‑day Britain, furiously retailing its own heritage, run by fill-ins and opportunists, a mobile waxwork museum living on tourism and memories.Are Tottenham doomed? Probably not. They have enough semi-interested players to retain a solid hold on 17th place. Although frustratingly for Premier League content addicts, even this has been degraded by repetition. Spurs could get relegated now and you would just keep scrolling.Are Liverpool on the verge of a renaissance? Probably not. The Jürgen Klopp golden era is beginning to look quite distant, surrounded on all sides by something a bit like the present. And, yes, Florian Wirtz is a very good footballer. He just can’t resist contact very well, which is non‑negotiable in the Premier League. He is going to be really good at Paris Saint-Gemain/Bayern Munich/Inter.View image in fullscreenManchester United have had a difficult start to the season under Michael Carrick.Photograph: Dennis Goodwin/ProSports/ShutterstockOtherwise, it is a case of stasis and a reliable, entertaining, homogenised product. Tactically, we can still get excited about small changes. If you analyse it deeply you may find a little more counterattack, Anthony Elanga running fast, an inverted winger discovering almost by accident he can also cross with his strong foot.It is a mark of how standardised the game has become that these are deemed things worth getting excited about. There is still only one elite level style, the Omniball template of the Cruyff-Michels-Guardiola-Gegenpressing school.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThis is skewed towards physicality over control in England, but it still produces football that can feel at times a bit like driving a brand new electric car: fun, high‑grade, but also endlessly repeatable. It seems possible some time soon that a robotic bait‑the‑press system will meet a robotic bait-averse system and in that moment football will just cease to exist, reduced to two banks of human units staring at each other across a strip of empty grass.There are two things the Premier League could really do with in the remaining 87% of its season. The nudge into greater physicality is exciting and distinct. It is notable how many games have been decided by duels, collisions, a sense of greater wanting-it. Or perhaps not so surprising when the players are at roughly the same technical level, where the only real point of difference is sustained physical power and competitive will.This is one reason whyBrighton’s defeat of Arsenal on Saturdayseemed so interesting. It is rare to see any reigning champions not just beaten, but outskilled and outmuscled. For 90 minutes, only one of these teams looked like genuine contenders for every trophy on offer.This is the second thing the league could really do with. Is it possible for one of the well-run middle class to sustain this level over a season and give us another Leicester or something close? Can Brighton just play like that every week?Long-range hits and goals galore: inside the Premier League’s return to chaos | Andrew BeasleyRead moreThere are obvious answers why not. One very good game against an ambushed Arsenal is not a 38-game slog. Brighton have a good squad, but also regular midweek football. Other teams will react and nullify your strengths. Also, and this is not a throwaway detail, Fabian Hürzeler is going to be on TalkSport for an hour on Tuesday just chatting football, which will now include how did you beat the champs and why are you third in the league.Nothing wrong with this. But it is an indicator of where we are. Hürzeler is 33. The entire job is essentially reinventing himself, just as all of the very good players at those middleweight clubs are auditioning for bigger clubs rather than dreaming of hauling them in, playing for the life-changing money a Champions League-level club will throw at them, motivated by a breezy and entirely logical collective individualism.Perhaps this is why one of the themes of the season has been a suspicion among fans of bigger clubs that their players don’t want it enough, that being outrun or outworked is a sign of soul sickness or debauched management. But it is also what keeps the league brutally strong, state of the art, and endlessly moreish for all its repeated story arcs. Come back soon Premier League mega-product. The comedown is already hitting.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeaguefeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Thomas Tuchel rocked by five key withdrawals from England squad | England | The Guardian
description: Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento are all out because of injury issues
Author: David Hytner
Headline: Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento are all out because of injury issues
Content: Cole Palmer has made only three England appearances under Thomas Tuchel and again has been ruled out of contention.Photograph: News Images/NurPhoto/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenCole Palmer has made only three England appearances under Thomas Tuchel and again has been ruled out of contention.Photograph: News Images/NurPhoto/ShutterstockEnglandThomas Tuchel rocked by five key withdrawals from England squadPalmer, Rice, Mainoo, Rashford and Livramento injuredJames Garner and Morgan Gibbs-White called-up as coverDavid HytnerMon 21 Sep 2026 09.39 EDTFirst published on Mon 21 Sep 2026 07.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThomas Tuchel has been rocked by a host of withdrawals from his England squad, with Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo,Marcus Rashfordand Tino Livramento all out because of injury. The head coach has called up James Garner and Morgan Gibbs‑White to boost his options for the upcoming Nations League programme.Tuchel gave Palmer a high-profile recall on Friday for the beginning of the two-year international cycle that he hopes will end in glory at Euro 2028. England are back in the top division of theNations Leagueand they kick off against Spain at Wembley on Saturday. They then play Czechia and Croatia away before returning to Wembley to face Czechia.Palmer has felt a minor muscle issue and, not for the first time under Tuchel, has been forced to make himself unavailable. The Chelsea midfielder, who has started the season in fine form, has made only three appearances under Tuchel. He was left out of the World Cup squad after his form ebbed last season and the head coach spoke at his squad announcement of a fresh opportunity for Palmer. That will have to wait. The 24-year-old has been a virtual ever‑present for Chelsea this season, contributing four goals and two assists in all competitions.‘Embrace the chaos’: Tuchel aims to harness England’s football cultureRead moreRice’s withdrawal is not a complete surprise given his workload for a number of seasons. He needed to manage a nerve issue in a hamstring in the second half of last season which also affected his lower back and caused the midfielder discomfort at the World Cup. He has started all of Arsenal’s Premier League matches so far this season – plus their Champions League opener against Napoli. It has been decided that a rest at this point is the wisest course of action.Mainoo was taken off after 80 minutes ofManchester United’s game at Fulham on Sunday; a move from the manager, Michael Carrick, that led to boos from the travelling support. The midfielder was in the World Cup squad but he was the only outfield player not to get a single minute on the pitch. Tuchel has said Mainoo’s lack of involvement was no slight on him, his ability or application levels. It was, instead, purely down to decisions that Tuchel took for technical reasons. The head coach had promised to give Mainoo minutes over the coming fortnight or so.Mainoo’s United teammate Rashford was substituted in the 77th minute of the Fulham game and was seen holding the area by the front of his hip and groin as he slowly walked off.Tuchel has always championed Rashford; he called him up when he named his first squad in March of last year when the player was struggling for form. Tuchel wanted to show Rashford that he believed in him and he has always included the 28‑year‑old when he has been available.Tuchel seemed to lose a bit of faith after Rashford played poorly against the Democratic Republic of the Congo in thelast 32 of the World Cup finalstournament over the summer. Thereafter, Tuchel barely used him until England’s semi-final exit against Argentina, giving him a couple of minutes as a stoppage-time substitute in that game but nothing more. He did play him for the first 45 minutes of the third-place playoff against France.Livramento was named in the World Cup squad only to sustain a calf injury in training on the eve of the tournament. The Newcastle full‑back had to fly home. He underwent surgery and returned for his club as a substitute against Bournemouth at the start of the month. He had a setback in training beforeNewcastle’s win against Hull on Saturdayand was not in the matchday squad. The 23-year-old is yet to start a game this season.Garner comes in as a central midfield replacement for Rice and Mainoo while Gibbs-White adds to Tuchel’s options in the No 10 position in the absence of Palmer. Tuchel also has Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers and Eberechi Eze as No 10s. The players are due to report on Tuesday to St George’s Park.Explore more on these topicsEnglandThomas TuchelMarcus RashfordNations LeagueSpainnewsShareReuse this content

title: Granit Xhaka admits to receiving fake Covid vaccination certificate in 2022 | Switzerland | The Guardian
description: Granit Xhaka has been withdrawn from Switzerland’s squad after he admitted receiving a fake Covid vaccination certificate in 2022
Author: Louise Taylor
Headline: Granit Xhaka has been withdrawn from Switzerland’s squad after he admitted receiving a fake Covid vaccination certificate in 2022
Content: Granit Xhaka has described obtaining a fake Covid vaccination certificate, at a time when he was still at Arsenal, as a ‘mistake’.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAView image in fullscreenGranit Xhaka has described obtaining a fake Covid vaccination certificate, at a time when he was still at Arsenal, as a ‘mistake’.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PASwitzerlandGranit Xhaka admits to receiving fake Covid vaccination certificate in 2022Sunderland captain withdrawn from Switzerland squadHe will be questioned by prosecutor’s office in LucerneLouise TaylorMon 21 Sep 2026 07.46 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGranit Xhaka has been withdrawn from Switzerland’s squad after he admitted receiving a fake Covid vaccination certificate in 2022. The Sunderland andSwitzerlandcaptain – who was an Arsenal player at the time – has apologised for this “mistake” and will sit out his country’s forthcoming four Nations League matches.Xhaka is poised to be questioned by the prosecutor’s office in Lucerne next week as it decides whether any criminal proceedings will be initiated regarding the alleged issue of a series of false Covid certificates by a doctor based in the Swiss city during the pandemic. The doctor, who was first investigated in 2023, has denied the allegations.In a statement issued via Instagram, Xhaka acknowledged he had decided not to be inoculated against the virus. “In recent days there has been much reporting about a matter from my past. I would like to address this personally,” he wrote. “At the time, I was personally very uncertain and had serious concerns regarding the Covid-19 vaccination. I felt deep distrust of the vaccine and was plagued by fear and uncertainty.“In this turbulent emotional state, I obtained a vaccination certificate instead of clarifying my open questions through the proper channels. Today I clearly see this was not the right course of action. It was a mistake. I am sorry. I take responsibility for this decision, am committed to investigating the matter and am co-operating with the relevant authorities.”Xhaka tested positive for Covid in September 2022 and the 33-year-old – he turns 34 on Sunday – did not feature in Switzerland’s internationals that month.A spokesperson for the Lucerne cantonal prosector’s office said: “The aim [of the inquiries] is to clarify whether there has been conduct relevant under criminal law in connection with the possible fraudulent obtaining of a false certification and/or document forgery.”Should charges be brought, Xhaka could face a heavy fine or, theoretically, a five-year prison sentence. However, the imposition of the latter sanction – or any sort of custodial punishment – is understood to be extremely unlikely.Given that Xhaka was with Arsenal in 2022, Sunderland have told the Guardian they are not commenting on the matter. The midfielder left north London to join Bayer Leverkusen in 2023 and arrived at the Stadium of Light two years later.Xhaka, who has been capped 152 times by Switzerland, will now miss the Nations League matches away to North Macedonia and Scotland and at home against Slovenia and North Macedonia.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe president of the Swiss Football Association, Peter Knabel, said: “Granit Xhaka approached us about the situation last [Sunday] night and told us he would admit it publicly and take responsibility. We welcome Granit taking this step and facing the consequences. We jointly concluded that it is in the team’s interests to complete the entire camp without him. Our priority now is to calm the situation.”Although the Swiss FA possess the power to hit Xhaka with a suspension from football – something they could ask Fifa to apply worldwide – that scenario is regarded as highly unlikely.Explore more on these topicsSwitzerlandnewsShareReuse this content

title: Ghosts of 2023 quelled after Dortmund return to the Bundesliga summit  | Bundesliga | The Guardian
description: It is probably a stretch to call BVB title contenders but Niko Kovac’s side maintained their 100% start against Stuttgart
Author: Andy Brassell
Headline: It is probably a stretch to call BVB title contenders but Niko Kovac’s side maintained their 100% start against Stuttgart
Content: Jobe Bellingham (centre) came off the Borussia Dortmund bench to set up the winner at Stuttgart.Photograph: Heiko Becker/ReutersView image in fullscreenJobe Bellingham (centre) came off the Borussia Dortmund bench to set up the winner at Stuttgart.Photograph: Heiko Becker/ReutersBundesligaGhosts of 2023 quelled after Dortmund return to the Bundesliga summitIt is probably a stretch to call BVB title contenders but Niko Kovac’s side maintained their 100% start against StuttgartAndy BrassellMon 21 Sep 2026 09.17 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 11.39 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBorussia Dortmund would probably rather not think about the last time that they topped the Bundesliga. It was in May 2023, just beforeall their dreams imploded, with black and yellow Deutscher Meister t-shirts – ‘German champions’ – for sale on the approach to Signal Iduna Park and cold beers at the ready. Now, that is no longer the most recent time Dortmund have led the pack.It’s four games, four wins to start this season and the Niko Kovac workout plan is hitting the spot. Saturday night’ssingle-goal win at Stuttgartwas a game that had the gravitas of a true Topspiel, if not quite the entertainment value of one. Kovac’s fingerprints were all over it. The conversation of whether his view of the game fits with BVB’s swashbuckling image will no doubt continue, but this was a case in point to show just how good Kovac has been for the club, and for the team.Champions Inter deny would-be title rivals Roma as Martínez haunts Gasperini | Nicky BandiniRead moreDortmund had taken four points from the two games against Sebastian Hoeness and hisStuttgartteam last season – and just as Kovac will not be oblivious to criticism of his side’s style, nor is Hoeness to whispers about his impressive team’s waning record against direct rivals – but were hardly overwhelmingly impressive either. It had been a huge improvement on the 2024-25 encounters with Stuttgart, in which BVB had been well beaten, twice, once under the short reign of Nuri Sahin and once in Kovac’s first game in charge, at which point he must have realised the mountainous task ahead of him.Here, in September 2026, was the clearest of markers of how far Dortmund have come under the former Croatia midfielder and how deeply his ideas have taken root. To see a Dortmund patient, poised and defensively competent enough to grind this game out is still a novelty, and they didn’t have a shot on target until Maximilian Beier prodded in the winner from an inviting ball in by substitute Jobe Bellingham. That Dortmund dealt with everything the home side had in response, with street smarts and limited fuss, was laudable. They made a very accomplished attacking forced look ordinary. “In a top match,” Stuttgart’s Hoeness later reflected, “decent and okay aren’t enough.”That Bellingham and Beier combined for the goal was noteworthy too; the former frequently rubbished for not being the equal of his generationally-talented elder brother and the latter another player who is simply underrated, both were brought in for big money and accordingly viewed with little patience. Their adaptability was striking, with Bellingham impacting off the bench and Beier thriving in a more advanced role. They are both Kovac’s type: young, willing, athletic and adaptable.View image in fullscreenNiko Kovac has been in charge of Borussia Dortmund since January 2025.Photograph: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/ShutterstockShould we call Dortmund contenders? That is, perhaps, a bit strong. But there is talk is about reducing the 16-point gap to Bayern that remained at the end of last season, and there were signs here that they may, at least, be capable of that. “It’s about annoying Bayern a bit”, is how Dortmund managing director Lars Ricken framed it, following the win at Stuttgart.Dortmund were never going to return to relevance and consistency by trying to relive the Jürgen Klopp years, or by trying to ape Bayern (and yes, both of those approaches have been attempted). To get into the position where they can face the hurt (and potential rewards) of 2023 all over again will take a while, and doesn’t just depend on them – it will take Bayern falling down a rung or two. They are at least climbing the right ladder though, slowly, steadily, and diligently.Quick GuideBundesliga resultsShowBayern Munich 7-0 Union Berlin, Stuttgart 0-1 Borussia Dortmund, Werder Bremen 3-2 Augsburg, Hamburg 2-1 Köln, Eintracht Frankfurt 2-2 Freiburg, Borussia Mönchengladbach 3-4 Mainz, Paderborn 3-1 Hoffenheim, Schalke 0-0 Elversberg, Bayer Leverkusen 2-0 RB LeipzigWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Talking pointsIt was only a matter of time and it was probably always going to happen against an ailing Union Berlin, who are enduring a horrible start to the season, butHarry Kane reached 100 Bundesliga goalson Friday night in his 98th game, so much faster than anyone in the league’s history. His double was almost a footnote on a night as Michael Olise scored a dazzling hat-trick, with Jamal Musiala and Ismaël Saibari also netting their first league goals of the season in a 7-0 shellacking. It was a good start to the club’s traditional celebration of Oktoberfest weekend.Bayern later mourned Peter Hermann, Jupp Heynckes’ popular assistant in the 2013 treble-winning season, who passed away on Saturday at the age of 73. Hermann was also emotionally commemorated at Leverkusen before kick-off on Sunday, having played in their 1979 promotion-winning team and having later served as assistant to Klaus Toppmöller at the helm of the celebrated 2002 Champions League finalists. Die Werkself paid fitting tribute on the field too as they beat RB Leipzig 2-0. The margins were fine, with Christopher Nkunku having an opener ruled out for the visitors before Patrik Schick put the home side ahead from a Miguel Gutiérrez cross. Gutiérrez, Álex Grimaldo’s nominal replacement, scored the second himself. Carles Martínez praised his team for “good balance between keeping the ball and playing forward”, while his opposite number Martín Demichelis has plenty to think about after a fourth straight away defeat.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenBayer Leverkusen players and fans hold a minute of silence for Peter Hermann.Photograph: Martin Meissner/APNever before had a team scored three times in successiveBundesligahome games and lost both of them but Borussia Mönchengladbach are managing to find a ledge beneath the edge. Gladbach made a bright start against Mainz (who are under interim coach Jan-Moritz Lichte) – with Florian Neuhaus scoring the opener on his return to the line-up, his first since May 2024 – but ended in defeat again, leaving them bottom, without a point. Alexander Blessin, a former St Pauli coach famed for his defensive work, is expected to arrive in an attempt to plug the leaks.Hamburg had gone into matchday four pointless and goalless but managed to squeeze past a Köln side who dominated them, with Yussuf Poulsen’s second goal for the club since arriving in summer 2025 proving decisive. It was an endorsement of their faith in head coach Merlin Polzin, who signed a contract extension this week despite that bad start and successive 5-0 defeats.There are comebacks and there are comebacks, and several coincided on the Weser as Werder Bremen continued their surprisingly good start to the season. They trailed 2-0 to Augsburg but were level after a Niclas Füllkrug netbuster but even better was around the corner, with Mitchell Weiser rattling in a perfect left-foot winner, deep into stoppage time, in his first home appearance after 16 months out with injury. It brought the former Bayern man to tears and his coach Daniel Thoune described it as “a goosebump moment”.All three promoted teams now have a win after Paderborn’s shock victory over Hoffenheim in Sunday’s late game, with veteran substitute Steffen Tigges sealing it with a header for his first top-flight goal since 2024. It was a third loss in four for Hoffenheim, who also suffered an embarrassing Europa League reverse at OFI Crete on Thursday.PosTeamPGDPts1Borussia Dortmund47122Bayern Munich412103Freiburg49104Augsburg4575Bayer Leverkusen4576Mainz4477Elversberg4178Werder Bremen4079RB Leipzig44610Eintracht Frankfurt4-1511Schalke 044-1512Paderborn4-2413Cologne4-3414Hoffenheim4-3315Stuttgart4-3316Hamburg4-11317Union Berlin4-13118Borussia M'gladbach4-100This article was amended on 21 September 2026. An earlier version said Werder Bremen defeated Wolfsburg; in fact, they beat Augsburg.Explore more on these topicsBundesligaBorussia DortmundStuttgartEuropean club footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Pierre Sage took Lens to new heights. His replacement left after six games | Ligue 1 | The Guardian
description: Lens finished second in Ligue 1 last season and won the Coupe de France. Building on that success is proving trickyBy Get French Football News
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Lens finished second in Ligue 1 last season and won the Coupe de France. Building on that success is proving trickyBy Get French Football News
Content: Lens were beaten 2-1 by Monaco on Friday in what was Yannick Cahuzac’s first game in charge.Photograph: Alunno Nicolas/ABACA/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenLens were beaten 2-1 by Monaco on Friday in what was Yannick Cahuzac’s first game in charge.Photograph: Alunno Nicolas/ABACA/ShutterstockGuardian Sport NetworkLigue 1Pierre Sage took Lens to new heights. His replacement left after six gamesLens finished second in Ligue 1 last season and won the Coupe de France. Building on that success is proving trickyByGet French Football NewsLuke EntwistleMon 21 Sep 2026 11.16 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 11.58 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt was under cover of darkness that Yannick Cahuzac took his place in theLensdugout at the Stade Louis II on Friday night. The lights dimmed as the players made their entrance and Cahuzac, who had been named interim manager just three days earlier, sat alone, leaning forward on a seat that Dino Toppmöller would have occupied if not for a dramatic turn of events last week.Cahuzac’s appointment, much like his entrance inMonaco, had a stealthy quality, as if he had always been there and the switching of the lights was mere confirmation of his presence. Cahuzac left Lorient, where he had been Olivier Pantaloni’s assistant, at the end of last season to return to Lens, where he had finished his playing career before working as Franck Haise’s assistant in the 2022–23 campaign.The last two seasons were grim for Spurs. This is as bad as it’s ever been | Jonathan WilsonRead moreHe was spoken about as a future No 1, but that was not the role he took in the summer. Cahuzac is still an apprentice who has not yet obtained his coaching qualifications so he returned to the club as an assistant to Toppmöller. The German had the unenviable task of succeeding Pierre Sage, who hastilydeparted to Crystal Palaceafter guiding Lens to a maiden Coupe de France triumph and a second-place finish in Ligue 1 last season.Lens were not expected to soar as high this season. Speaking in the summer, the club’s sporting director, Jean-Louis Leca, said they were “not a Champions League club” and that an eighth-place finish inLigue 1would represent success. Toppmöller’s first game in charge brought silverware as Lens beat PSG in the Trophée des Champions; his first Ligue 1 game was a resounding 5-2 win over Auxerre; and his side took all three points away to Slavia Prague in their first Champions League game – not a bad start after a summer of upheaval and the departure of several important players.Results have dipped in recent weeks but expectations were being met. Hence the shock last week when it was announced that the German had left the club by mutual consent. Having taken charge of just six games, Toppmöller is Lens’s shortest-serving manager since the second world war. His exit says more about the club than it does the man. Explaining the parting of ways, the chief executive, Benjamin Parrot, revealed a divide, not necessarily between Toppmöller and his squad, but rather within the staff itself.“Even before the Trophée des Champions, we felt, within the staff, that there was a French group and then a more international group,” said Parrot. Toppmöller brought two assistants with him. Lens tried to sack one of them, Nelson Morgado, but Toppmöller stayed loyal to his assistant and refused to accept his dismissal. He left and Cahuzac stepped up in his place.View image in fullscreenParis Brunner and Denis Zakaria embrace after Monaco take the lead in their win against Lens.Photograph: Alunno Nicolas/Abaca/ShutterstockCahuzac was touted as Toppmöller’s successor before he had even settled at the club. That can’t be a healthy environment for any new manager. Perhaps the writing was always on the wall for Toppmöller, especially given that Leca – Cahuzac’s close friend and former teammate at Bastia – is the club’s sporting director. Leca knows how it looks. “Yes, he is my friend, but inside these walls he isn’t my friend. Inside these walls, I am his line manager,” said Leca.To suggest that Cahuzac’s appointment is pure nepotism is unfair. Lorient were one of the most tactically interesting teams in Ligue 1 last season and while Pantaloni – who was nominated for the manager-of-the-season award – earned most of the plaudits, Cahuzac played a key role too. He also knows the club, having played for them for three seasons and worked under Haise as an assistant.His first game in charge, against Monaco, did not begin well. The hosts were 1-0 up at half-time but they had the ball in the Lens net on three occasions, denied by the assistant referee’s flag. Cahuzac changed tactics at the interval, which helped, and Matthieu Udol headed in a deserved equaliser. Franjo Ivanovic and Thorgan Hazard had chances as Lenspushed for a winner. In the end, it was a Lens player who scored but, unfortunately for Jonathan Gradit, it was into his own net.So, Cahuzac’s tenure begins with a valiant 2-1 defeat. The 41-year-old was a pitbull of a player but he was almost inert in his dugout. He stood like a statue, with his hand on his chin in a pensive pose that exuded a studious serenity. After the turbulent week Lens have had, the club need a sense of calm.Quick GuideLigue 1 resultsShowAuxerre 2-1 BrestNice 2-1 LilleMarseille 1-2 PSGParis FC 2-1 StrasbourgAngers 2-0 TroyesLe Mans 2-1 LorientLyon 4-0 RennesToulouse 3-2 Le HavreMonaco 2-1 LensWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Talking pointsOn the topic of messy break-ups, there was an unhappy reunion between Liam Rosenior and Strasbourg on Saturday. The pair had not met since Rosenior was hurried out the doorto join sister club Chelseain January. There is no love lost. The Englishman led Paris FC to a 2-1 win, continuing his unbeaten run since returning to Ligue 1 this summer. He celebrated the win in front of the travelling Strasbourg fans, a response, Rosenior said, to insulting chants about his family from the away end. An unsavoury confrontation between both sets of players and staff ensued. Rosenior said the chants had gone “too far” and that “celebrating like that was clearly a message”. His players also sent a message, confirming that they are in the mix for Champions League qualification.View image in fullscreenLiam Rosenior celebrated Paris FC’s win in front of the travelling Strasbourg fans.Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/Zuma Press Wire/ShutterstockPSG beatMarseille2-1 in aClassiquethat encapsulated the clubs’ seasons so far; both are struggling. For PSG, the points are at least now flowing. Ferran Torres continues to prove a fine signing. He came off the bench to score the opening goal. Marquinhos redeemed himself for his own goal in this fixture last season, which gave Marseille their first win over PSG at the Vélodrome in Ligue 1 in 14 years. That feels like a long time ago now. The concerns for Marseille only deepen. There were bright moments, notably Angel Gomes’s equaliser, but Bruno Génésio’s side have now lost four of their first five league matches. “A Ligue 2 project?” read a banner from the home fans. They go into the international break in the relegation zone.Despite the game being briefly suspended after the home fans unfurled an insulting banner that targeted their fierce rivals Saint-Étienne, Lyon made a statement with a 4-0 win overRennes. They rotated in their midweek Europa League win over Anderlecht, a clear but disappointing sign of where their priorities lie. It paid off, however. Rennes fielded a stronger side against Sturm Graz but did not take the three points, and their striker Esteban Lepaul was consequently not involved from the start against Lyon. A full-strength Lyon made short work of Franck Haise’s side, who may struggle to balance their European and league commitments. Rennes did not lay a glove on Lyon, whose own fans posed the greatest threat.PosTeamPGDPts1Monaco55132Lyon58113Paris FC55114Lille54105Rennes5-1106PSG5187Angers5178Strasbourg5079Le Mans50610Auxerre5-5611Brest5-1512Lorient5-1513Toulouse5-2514Nice5-3515Lens50416Troyes5-7417Marseille5-1318Le Havre5-32This is an article byGet French Football NewsExplore more on these topicsLigue 1Guardian Sport NetworkEuropean club footballLensMarseilleParis Saint-GermainMonacoLyonfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: WSL talking points: Arsenal’s attacking woes and Goodwin makes England case | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: The Gunners are held to a second home draw in two weeks, while Spurs smash Palace 7-0 to maintain strong start
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: The Gunners are held to a second home draw in two weeks, while Spurs smash Palace 7-0 to maintain strong start
Content: Arsenal’s Leah Williamson, Tottenham’s Olivia Holdt, and London City Lionesses Isobel Goodwin.Composite: Shutterstock, GettyView image in fullscreenArsenal’s Leah Williamson, Tottenham’s Olivia Holdt, and London City Lionesses Isobel Goodwin.Composite: Shutterstock, GettyWomen's Super LeagueWSL talking points: Arsenal’s attacking woes and Goodwin makes England caseGunners are held to second home draw in two weeks, while Spurs smash Palace 7-0 to maintain strong startTom Garry,Sophie Downey,Réshma Raoand Mitul SamjiMon 21 Sep 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 11.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1Why do Arsenal struggle to break down low blocks?After being unable to find a way through Crystal Palace’s backline last time out, Arsenal were again frustrated at home in a draw with Manchester United on Saturday and Renée Slegers was asked post-match about how her team can turn their dominance of possession and territory into more goals. It could have been worse, of course, if Smilla Holmberg had not made it 1-1 in the 95th minute. “It’s not one thing, it’s a combination of things,” Slegers said. “It’s a cocktail of things, there are some details in decision making, some details in the technical execution. It’s also the ruthlessness in front of goal but I know the players want it and they want to do that, they want to execute for Arsenal.”Tom GarryMatch report: Arsenal 1-1 Manchester United2A good win for Lionesses, Goodwin for England?Just over a week before Sarina Wiegman names her Lionesses squad for October’s World Cup playoff tie against Greece, the England Under-23 international Isobel Goodwin did her chances of a first senior selection no harm at all, as she scored twice forLondon City Lionessesin a comprehensive 4-1 victory at Charlton. The 23-year-old, who linked up well with Alexia Putellas, scored five times in the WSL last term but will be keen to exceed that this season and impress Wiegman, particularly at a time when Chelsea’s Aggie Beever-Jones has been out with a minor ankle injury and Arsenal’s Michelle Agyemang is still returning from her ACL. Wiegman may be considering alternative options for a backup striker to Alessia Russo for these key fixtures.TG3Hemp adds goals to her repertoireShe was the WSL’s leading assist-provider in the 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons and supplied the joint-second highest number of assists last season, but goals were not coming regularly for the England winger Lauren Hemp, who had not scored in the WSL since last November until she decisively found the net twice on Friday night in a 4-2 win over Liverpool. The Manchester City manager, Andrée Jeglertz, heaped praise on Hemp as he told Sky Sports: “She’s an amazing player. I don’t know what she’s made of, because she just loves to be on the field and looks like she has so much energy. She’s a gamechanger.” Hemp nearly had a hat-trick but she saw an early, rising strike tipped over the bar by Khiara Keating.TGMatch report: Manchester City 4-2 LiverpoolView image in fullscreenManchester City’s Lauren Hemp scores against Liverpool.Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock4Potter shines at the heart of Chelsea’s midfieldThere has been plenty of debate in recent months about the future of young English players in theWSL and whether they are being hampered by limited opportunities. England’s Lexi Potter, however, is one young talent who has been catching the eye at the heart of Chelsea’s midfield. The 2-0 win over Birmingham City was her second start in as many matches and she produced yet another assured performance. The 20-year-old’s calmness and ability to work in tight spaces enables her to escape pressure while the timing of her runs into the box is a huge asset. She opened the scoring at Stamford Bridge by being alert to the second ball in the area while her burgeoning relationship with Keira Walsh has been notable. “They understand each other, and even when they are on the pitch and they close their eyes, they know where each other is,” Sonia Bompastor told Chelsea media. Like Goodwin, may she have done enough to catch Wiegman’s eye?Sophie Downeyskip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion5Another own goal sends Everton up to fifthHow do you register six points without scoring a goal? Everton completed this remarkable feat after a late winner at West Ham – an own goal from defender Laia Codina – gave them all three points. It was the second time in as many weeks that a touch from an opponent handed them a victory but it will not matter to Scott Phelan’s side who sit pretty at fifth in the table. It was an even affair for the most parts in Dagenham with both setups nullifying the other. The Toffees looked defensively resilient, handling the threat of Kelly Gago and Viviane Asseyi comfortably. Down the other end, West Ham did the same with the visitors’ attack. Both had an equal share of possession, both had similar xGs and both registered just three shots on target. Everton’s ability to finish strongly, however, was the difference maker. Phelan turned to his bench and they were able to ratchet up the pressure with Yuka Momiki providing the delivery for the winner.SDView image in fullscreenRuby Mace celebrates after Laia Codina of West Ham (not pictured) scores an own goal.Photograph: James Fearn/Getty Images6Holdt ignites Spurs on way to routOlivia Holdt marked her first start of the season by scoring a hat-trick as Spurs turned a dominant but goalless first half into a 7-0 win at Crystal Palace. Palace’s task was made harder when Fuka Tsunoda was sent off in the seventh minute following a reckless challenge on Cathinka Tandberg, but Spurs initially struggled to break down a side defending deep. “When they got the red card, I was thinking this could actually be tougher for us,” Holdt said. At half-time, the Spurs manager, Martin Ho, asked his players to get more bodies into the box. Holdt had completed her hat-trick by the 73rd minute as Spurs finally found the ruthlessness that had been missing.Mitul Samji7Brighton’s lack of clinical edge proves costlyBrighton may have had 25 shots, eight on target and an xG of 3.17, but they were forced to settle for a 1-1 draw against Aston Villa after failing to make their dominance count. Gabby George’s first goal for the club gave them a deserved lead in the 31st minute, but they could not find a second despite creating 15 chances. The result was made all the more frustrating by the manner of Villa’s equaliser in the 89th minute, with Brighton unable to defend a corner. The result leaves the new manager, Arturo Ruiz, still searching for their first win of the season. “Here in our stadium, in these kinds of games we cannot lose two points,” he said. “We need to get three points in 100% of these games.” The performance was encouraging, but the finishing was not.Réshma RaoPosTeamPGDPts1Man City Women3792Tottenham Hotspur Women3973Chelsea Women3774London City Lionesses3365Everton Women3166Arsenal Women3157Liverpool FC Women3248Crystal Palace Women3-649West Ham Women3-2310Brighton & Hove Albion Women3-1211Aston Villa Women3-3212Birmingham City Women3-4113Man Utd Women3-6114Charlton Women3-80Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueWomen's footballArsenal WomenManchester United WomenLondon City LionessesCharlton WomenManchester City WomenfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Harry Brook says Brydon Carse ‘just needs time away from the international scene’ | Cricket | The Guardian
description: England’s white-ball captain has said the fast bowler Brydon Carse ‘is working on a few things’, on the eve of the one-day international series against Sri Lanka
Author: Ali Martin
Headline: England’s white-ball captain has said the fast bowler Brydon Carse ‘is working on a few things’, on the eve of the one-day international series against Sri Lanka
Content: The England bowler Brydon Carse is still under investigation by cricket’s authorities.Photograph: Robbie Stephenson/PAView image in fullscreenThe England bowler Brydon Carse is still under investigation by cricket’s authorities.Photograph: Robbie Stephenson/PACricketHarry Brook says Brydon Carse ‘just needs time away from the international scene’Bowler ‘is working on a few things’England v Sri Lanka ODIs come a year before World CupAli MartinMon 21 Sep 2026 12.25 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 15.21 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHarry Brook is hopeful that Brydon Carse will break back into his England white-ball teams once the fast bowler is clear of his disciplinary proceedings, describing him as a “very good mate” who is “working on a few things behind the scenes”.Carse discovered recently he willnot face a criminal chargefor thelate-night incident in Derbylast month that led to him being briefly handcuffed. But while technically available for selection, the 31‑year‑old has not featured in England’s squads since that night as he awaits the outcome of an investigation by the Cricket Regulator.McCullum hails Brook’s captaincy as England move top of T20 world rankingsRead moreAsked before Tuesday’s first one‑day international against Sri Lanka at Chester-le-Street about the prospect of Carse returning down the line, Brook, England’s white-ball captain, replied: “He’s a very good cricketer. He’s been bowling extremely well for Durham. When his time for selection is up, that will be a debate.“I’m very good mates with Carsey. I’ve spoken a lot with him. Those conversations are private. I think he just needs time away from the international scene. He’s working on a few things behind the scenes and hopefully he’ll be ready at some point in the future.”More broadly, Brook believes the call for greater off-field professionalism has permeated through the England squads, both from Brendon McCullum, the white-ball head coach, and Stephen Fleming ahead of his new role with the Test side.Brook, who fell short of standards himselfwhen punched by a nightclub bouncer in New Zealand last winter, said: “The words Baz [McCullum] saidthe other day[were that] we want to be one of the fittest and strongest teams in the world. And to be able to do that we need to be preparing well on and off the field.”On top of Carse’s absence, England are missing Jacob Bethell and Sam Curran because of injury. Adil Rashid, another first-choice pick, will also miss the first match – and potentially the series – as he awaits scan results on an issue with his bowling hand sustained during the whitewash-sealing T20 winat Old Trafford on Saturday.View image in fullscreenAs well as captaining the white-ball teams, Harry Brook (centre) is a key figure in the Test team now under the direction of the new head coach, Stephen Fleming (right),Photograph: Matt West/ShutterstockIn come Tom Banton to open and Jamie Overton with the ball, while Rehan Ahmed, 16 years younger than Rashid at 22, gets his chance as the team’s wrist-spinner. Will Jacks, the new vice-captain, and Joe Root will provide finger-spin options.England go into the series opener with momentum from the 3-0 sweep of Sri Lanka that took themto No 1 in the T20 rankings. However their ODI ranking of seventh – one spot below the tourists – shows there is work to be done in 50-over cricket, despite having come from 1-0 down to win both their series this year.Brook said: “We’ve gone undefeated in the T20s and I think we can take a hell of a lot of confidence from that going into this ODI series. It’s more of the same. As a squad and a unit, we’re trying to play a higher-octane style of cricket and we’re really trying to put them under pressure with bat and ball.”The continued deployment of Jofra Archer and Josh Tongue at the end of a long, all-format summer for the pair is also notable. The next 12 months are about building towards the 50-over World Cup in southern Africa, meaning full-strength ODI XIs where possible and T20 series likely to involve more squad rotation.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAs an all-format player but one who limits his franchise cricket to the Hundred, Brook intends to plough through. His stated aim in this ODI series is improved strike-rotation during middle overs and playing against spin in particular, having enjoyed the input of Kevin Pietersen asthe team’s new white-ball mentor.View image in fullscreenTom Banton will be Ben Duckett’s sixth ODI opening partner since the start of 2025.Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/ShutterstockAsked if Pietersen has also helped him to deal with criticism over shot selection and some of his brain fades in the past, Brook replied: “I haven’t had those conversations with him yet, but I’m sure it will come up at some point.“I think the way I’ve performed in my career so far, it’s almost a compliment to get those opinions. I’ll be trying my hardest to be the best player I can possibly be.”While Pietersen is with the senior white-ball side, his former England teammate Jonathan Trott has been named as head coach of the England Lions for tours of the Caribbean, South Africa and Sri Lanka this winter. Trott, who previously coached Afghanistan, replacesAndrew Flintoff after he stood down last month.Explore more on these topicsCricketHarry BrookEngland cricket teamSri Lanka cricket teamKevin PietersennewsShareReuse this content

title: Collingwood’s Nick Daicos wins first Brownlow medal with record 47 votes | AFL | The Guardian
description: Midfielder beats previous record of 45 votes, as he finished ahead of Marcus Bontempelli and Bailey Smith
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Midfielder beats previous record of 45 votes, as he finished ahead of Marcus Bontempelli and Bailey Smith
Content: Collingwood’s Nick Daicos reacts after winning the Brownlow medal.Photograph: Quinn Rooney/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCollingwood’s Nick Daicos reacts after winning the Brownlow medal.Photograph: Quinn Rooney/Getty ImagesAFLCollingwood’s Nick Daicos wins first Brownlow medal with record 47 votesMidfielder beats previous record of 45 votesMarcus Bontempelli and Bailey Smith are runners-upAustralian Associated PressMon 21 Sep 2026 08.47 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 18.44 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCollingwood star Nick Daicos has finally claimed his first Brownlow medal with a record-breaking 47 votes sealing a runaway victory, and relief for the brilliant Magpie.The 23-year-old surged to a perfect nine votes from his first three games, led from round 11, then registered six consecutive best-on-ground performances between rounds 15 and 20 to seal victory by round 21.AFL grand final 2026: ultimate guide to the flag decider between Fremantle and BrisbaneRead moreDaicos won the AFL’s greatest individual honour from Geelong star Bailey Smith (36) and Western Bulldogs champion Marcus Bontempelli (34).The Magpie had 13 three-vote performances and beat the previous votes record of 45 set by Carlton champion Patrick Cripps in 2024.Daicos, the son of Magpies great Peter Daicos, conceded he was relieved, having finally prevailed after runner-up finishes in the past two seasons, a third placing in 2023 and an eighth place in his debut year of 2022.“I’ve just learned not to trust the the betting markets, to be honest,” Daicos said at Monday night’s vote count. “But no, there is [relief]. It’s a massive award, and I’m so privileged to be here. I can’t believe I’m a Brownlow medallist, to be honest.”The dynamic midfielder had already snared the AFL Players Association and AFL Coaches Association player-of-the-year awards.It was the fourth consecutive year that Daicos was favourite, and with the umpires able to consult statistics for the first time, the star Magpie was irresistible. Daicos averaged 34.9 disposals, 5.7 clearances, 6.7 inside-50s and 1.1 goals.The brilliant playmaker was edged out by Gold Coast’s Matt Rowell last year and Cripps the year before, when Daicos polled 38 votes.View image in fullscreenDaicos addresses the crowd at Crown Palladium in Melbourne.Photograph: Joel Carrett/AAPDaicos, the Collingwood vice-captain widely expected to be named skipper next season, is the club’s 10th Brownlow medallist and first since Dane Swan in 2011.The 23-year-old, an “absolute nuffy” turned Collingwood prodigy, conceded he had struggled with expectation and scrutiny, as the son of a Collingwood great and younger brother of fellow Magpie Josh.“Pretty quickly, it did get a little bit overwhelming playing for Collingwood and having Dad play, Josh play, and being in the spotlight all the time,” Daicos said. “And it’s probably something I feel I’ve pushed away as the years have gone on and shied away from.“And I wouldn’t say struggled with, but I’ve definitely battled with it at times, and deleted social media, tried to stay off that stuff, and just give myself a little break where I can. But at the same time, I’m so bloody privileged to be in the position I’m in.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toFrom the Pocket: AFL WeeklyJonathan Horn brings expert analysis on the week's biggest AFL storiesEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMelbourne skipper Max Gawn (28) was fourth with three players tied for fifth: Brisbane star Will Ashcroft (27), Carlton’s two-time winner Patrick Cripps (27) and North Melbourne’s Harry Sheezel (27).Sheezel wasn’t even in the 40-man All-Australian squad.Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, set to join Bontempelli at the Bulldogs next season, was among the contenders before his late-season ankle injury ended his campaign early. He finished on 26.Patrick Dangerfield drew level with Gary Ablett Jnr on 262 career votes, the most ever.Sydney stars Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner weren’t in the room as they polled 26 and 12 votes respectively.The pair were among five Swans stood down by Sydney for breaching club standards and weren’t invited to the Brownlow function at Crown Palladium, but remained eligible for the award.Brisbane’s Conor McKenna won goal of the year while Hawthorn dynamo Nick Watson was awarded mark of the year.Explore more on these topicsAFLCollingwoodAustralian rules footballAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Shaun Edwards finally lands England coaching role after joining Red Roses | Rugby union | The Guardian
description: Defence guru Shaun Edwards will take his first post in women’s rugby after being brought on board as a consultant by England’s head coach, John Mitchell
Author: Sarah Rendell
Headline: Defence guru Shaun Edwards will take his first post in women’s rugby after being brought on board as a consultant by England’s head coach, John Mitchell
Content: Shaun Edwards won three Six Nations’ titles with France and four, including two Grand Slams, with the Welsh men’s team.Photograph: RFUView image in fullscreenShaun Edwards won three Six Nations’ titles with France and four, including two Grand Slams, with the Welsh men’s team.Photograph: RFURugby unionShaun Edwards finally lands England coaching role after joining Red RosesDefence guru left France men’s team in JuneEdwards will work as a consultant for duration of WXVSarah RendellMon 21 Sep 2026 06.32 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe defence guru Shaun Edwards has joined the Red Roses coaching setup in a consultancy role until the end of the WXV Global Series.The former Wales and France men’s coach has not had a role in women’s rugby before but has been brought on board with the Red Roses head coach, John Mitchell, describing his credentials as “exceptional” in the highest echelons of the sport.Ellie Kildunne: ‘I have had to look in the mirror quite a lot and stick to my values’Read moreThe 59-year-old Edwards is already in situ and will help the team as they prepare to take on New Zealand at Allianz Stadium this Saturday before travelling next month with the squad to Canada and the US.Edwards, who played rugby league for Wigan Warriors and Great Britain, left his role with France in June after more than six years when Fabien Galthié restructured the backroom staff.Mitchell said: “Since his time with France ended, we have had a conversation about our game, and he expressed an interest in working in an international women’s setup for the first time. He has a huge amount of respect for the Red Roses and what we stand for; he sees it as a privilege to join our environment.“His coaching credentials are exceptional and his experience at the highest level of the game speaks for itself. Defensively, Sarah Hunter [England’s defence coach] is relishing the opportunity to learn from him, alongside the rest of our coaching group, as we head into another exciting Test match against New Zealand. Shaun will add to the programme and provide incredible value to the girls over the remainder of the WXV Global Series.”Edwards began his coaching career in rugby union at the Premiership club Wasps, first joining as a defence and backs coach in 2001. He was promoted to head coach in 2005 and the club won the Heineken Cup and Premiership during his tenure. He then moved to Wales as a defence coach in 2011 and won four Six Nations titles, three of which were grand slams, alongside the head coach Warren Gatland.Edwards signed on as the France defence coach in 2020 and won three Six Nations titles with the team. He cannot win a trophy with the Red Roses as the WXV is a series of matches with no silverware. But he can help to get their victory record back on track after their 39-game winning run came to an end last Saturday in a26-26 draw against Canada.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionEngland will play the Black Ferns – who were the last team to beat the Red Roses, in the World Cup final in 2022 – in front of more than 50,000 this weekend.Explore more on these topicsRugby unionEngland women's rugby union teamWomen's rugby unionnewsShareReuse this content

title: Thirteen-year-old swim sensation sets women’s 200m butterfly record at Asian Games | Sport | The Guardian
description: Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi wins the first major title of her young career – but says her performance was ‘only so-so’
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi wins the first major title of her young career – but says her performance was ‘only so-so’
Content: China’s gold medallist Yu Zidi set a new record in the Asian Games 200m women’s butterfly race with a time of 2min 05.08sec.Photograph: Yuichi Yamazaki/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenChina’s gold medallist Yu Zidi set a new record in the Asian Games 200m women’s butterfly race with a time of 2min 05.08sec.Photograph: Yuichi Yamazaki/AFP/Getty ImagesSportThirteen-year-old swim sensation sets women’s 200m butterfly record at Asian GamesChinese swimmer Yu Zidi wins the first major title of her young career – but says her performance was ‘only so-so’Agence France-PresseSun 20 Sep 2026 23.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe 13-year-old Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi set an Asian Games record as she scorched to gold on Sunday’s first full day of competition.The schoolgirl, who turns 14 next month, took the women’s 200m butterfly crown in a Games-record 2min 05.08sec.It was the first major title of her young career, less than two years out from the Los Angeles Olympics.“It was only so-so,” a smiling Yu said after receiving her medal.View image in fullscreenYu Zidi competes in the women’s 200-metre individual medley heats at the Asian Games in Tokyo, Japan.Photograph: Hiro Komae/APYu became the youngest medallist in swimming world championships history last year when shetook home relay bronze aged 12.Balletic hits and bicycle kicks: Teqball comes of age at the Asian GamesRead moreSwimming is one of three sports at the Games taking place in Tokyo, where a typhoon is due to blow in, with the rest of the Games unfolding in Nagoya and Aichi prefecture.China is expected to be the pre-eminent power in the pool, on day one clinching six of the seven titles on offer.The Games were officially opened on Saturday by Emperor Naruhito.For the next two weeks, athletes will compete in more than 40 sports before closing on 4 October.The Games has 2028 Olympics places up for grabs but have been dogged by a series of problems in the buildup.Accommodating the more than 11,000 athletes and 6,000 officials has stretched organisers to the limit after they decided not to have a traditional athletes’ village to save money. Competitors are instead staying in a combination of temporary container-style huts, hotels and on the Costa Serena cruise ship.The International Olympic Committee president, Kirsty Coventry, called the temporary huts “beautiful” on Sunday after looking around – but conceded they were “a little tighter” than similar accommodation at the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics this year.Japanese organisers will be desperate for the sport to take over from a troubled lead-in that included complaints about the accommodation and a shortage of rooms.However, an incoming typhoon that soaked Tokyo on Sunday could cause more problems.The Tokyo venue hosting equestrian was closed because of the weather. The competition is now due to start on Tuesday, a day later than originally planned.The full force of Typhoon Dujuan will not be felt until Monday, with Tokyo expected to be hit with strong winds and heavy rain.Nagoya will not be in the storm’s immediate path but wet weather is forecast there too.Iran celebrated wildly after beating China 79-70 to win men’s basketball bronze.South Korea won basketball gold, silencing the home crowd with a 67-57 win over Japan.In other sports, Smriti Mandhana became the highest run-scorer in women’s T20 international cricket as India crushed Bangladesh by 114 runs in the semi-finals, with fellow opener Shafali Verma hitting her maiden hundred.India will face Sri Lanka in Tuesday’s final, unless the weather intervenes.Explore more on these topicsSportChinaJapanBasketballnewsShareReuse this content

title: NRL open investigation into fans after top referee pelted with rubbish at Eden Park | NRL | The Guardian
description: The NRL has threatened to ban fans who peppered referee Ashley Klein with projectiles, with the integrity unit investigating the aftermath of the Eden Park clash.
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The NRL has threatened to ban fans who peppered referee Ashley Klein with projectiles, with the integrity unit investigating the aftermath of the Eden Park clash.
Content: Referee Ashley Klein during the NRL semi-final between New Zealand Warriors and Newcastle Knights at Eden Park.Photograph: Andrew Cornaga/AAPView image in fullscreenReferee Ashley Klein during the NRL semi-final between New Zealand Warriors and Newcastle Knights at Eden Park.Photograph: Andrew Cornaga/AAPNRLNRL open investigation into fans after top referee pelted with rubbish at Eden ParkAshley Klein targeted after Warriors’ season ended by KnightsOfficial had to be protected by security on way off pitch in AucklandAustralian Associated PressSun 20 Sep 2026 22.37 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTheNRLhas threatened to ban fans who peppered referee Ashley Klein with projectiles, with the integrity unit investigating the aftermath of the Eden Park clash.Vision from after full-time in Newcastle’s 12-10 win over the Warriors on Sunday showed Klein being hit with a raft of bottles, cups and rubbish as he walked from the field.The footage shows Klein having to be protected by security, as fans abused the veteran referee and projectiles rained down on him.No more ‘Mark doing freaky things’ as Nawaqanitawase’s NRL farewell loomsRead moreThe NRL immediately launched an investigation into potential breaches of their spectators’ code of conduct. An Integrity Unit investigator had been at the ground.“If found guilty, they will be banned for a period of time from attending NRL games,” ARL Commission chairman Peter V’landys told AAP.Auckland police have since confirmed that no arrests were made, with “no issues to note” other than two pitch invaders.Sunday’s crowd of 48,511 marked the biggest ever for a rugby league match in New Zealand, after the NRL made the call to move the game from Mt Smart.The fan abuse came after two contentious calls went against the Warriors late in the match, including a decision not to penalise Tyson Frizell for an escort in the dying minutes.View image in fullscreenNewcastle Knights players celebrate winning the semi-final match in Auckland.Photograph: Andrew Cornaga/AAPWarriors great Shaun Johnson hit out at the fan’s response after the match, labelling it “embarrassing”.“It leaves a bit of a sour taste in your mouth, what has been an unbelievable night with the colours, the energy, the happiness and celebration,” Johnson said on Sky NZ’s coverage. “But there is just no need for it. It’s just embarrassing.“Ashley Klein has probably refereed the best game of rugby league I have seen in a long time tonight. He didn’t take any gamesmanship in terms of people laying down. He didn’t let people approach him whinging.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“He didn’t make the game about him. He let the players come and play and they dictated the outcome.”Warriors coach Andrew Webster had vented his frustration in the post-match press conference, highlighting a bunker strip call on Te Maire Martin and the decision not to penalise Frizell for a possible escort on Leka Halasima“The last one, two points would have drawn the game, he is going across Leka, pretending to try and catch the ball which they’ve told us you can’t do,” Webster said.The incident comes afterAFL umpires also had cans thrown at themwhile leaving the MCG after Hawthorn’s tight loss to Brisbane in Saturday night’s preliminary final.The AFL has also condemned the behaviour and warned of minimum five-year bans for any fans found responsible.Explore more on these topicsNRLRugby leagueAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Nvidia boss says there is ‘0% chance’ AI destroys the world by 2030 | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
description: Jensen Huang dismisses warnings from former Anthropic researcher and others as ‘doomsday narratives’
Author: Mark Sweney
Headline: Jensen Huang dismisses warnings from former Anthropic researcher and others as ‘doomsday narratives’
Content: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang said predictions of an extinction-level event caused by AI were ‘not grounded in science’.Photograph: Manami Yamada/ReutersView image in fullscreenNvidia’s Jensen Huang said predictions of an extinction-level event caused by AI were ‘not grounded in science’.Photograph: Manami Yamada/ReutersAI (artificial intelligence)Nvidia boss says there is ‘0% chance’ AI destroys the world by 2030Jensen Huang dismisses warnings from former Anthropic researcher and others as ‘doomsday narratives’Mark SweneyandRobert BoothMon 21 Sep 2026 06.31 EDTFirst published on Mon 21 Sep 2026 03.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe boss of the chipmakerNvidiahas said AI will not develop to a point that will lead to the extinction of the human race within a few years, rejecting such assertions as overblown “doomsday narratives”.Jensen Huang, the co-founder and chief executive of the $5tn AI chipmaker, said the claims made on social media by the former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon that AI could become “superhuman” andkill off humanitywithin the decade were “irresponsible”.“2030 is not going to be the end of the world. There is 0% chance that’s going to be the end of the world,” Huang said in an interview with CBS News. “Scaring people is unnecessary. It is irresponsible.”AI slowdown calls justified but collapse of bubble may be more immediate threat | Heather StewartRead moreCoxon’s remarks, which were backed by two other researchers at the maker of the AI system Claude, prompted an international debate about the dangers and lack of oversight of AI as companies race to develop ever more powerful models.US lawmakers havecriticised AI companies over the risksand Anthropic published a threat intelligence report detailing how criminals, state-sponsored groups, spyware vendors, scientists and propagandists have tried to use its powerful AI models to design missiles and bombs, create deadly pathogens and spy on dissidents.Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, Sam Altman, the boss of the ChatGPT maker OpenAI, and Elon Musk have called for development of the technology to be slowed down.However, Donald Trump has dismissed anxiety over the AI development as a“hoax” and a “conspiracy”, adding that a slowdown could give China the edge.On Sunday, Scott Bessent, the US Treasury secretary, said the US and China had agreed toset up an AI dialogue mechanismto alert each other to help contain the technology’s potential dangers.Huang said predictions of an extinction-level event caused by AI were “not grounded in science”.Huang also claimed AI companies’ recent calls for national and international safety regulation aim to duck existing laws that would hold them to account.Citing recent cases where AI companies including Anthropic and OpenAI triggered cybersecurity incidents during testing, he said there were plenty of laws to tackle the problems.“You have cybersecurity unauthorised entry laws, you have damage liabilities … if your product does harm, if your product doesn’t perform as you promised, and if you entered into contracts with companies for service level agreements, there are plenty of laws associated with that. My point is, apply those first. And don’t let this doomsday narrative cause somebody to relieve them of the laws that currently exist.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHe continued: “Now, go and read between the lines. They’re actually not asking for more laws. They’re asking to be relieved of the laws we do have. And I think that’s a problem.”On Monday the the Tony Blair Institute (TBI) thinktank published a paper arguing that countries risk “profound and compounding disadvantage” if they fail to embrace AI and fall behind other nations.However, it also warned that the institutions meant to support the choices leaders would have to makewere not equipped to do so.“The previous [industrial] revolution transformed our world over generations, AI will do so within a decade,” said Tony Blair in aforeword to the paper. “New capabilities are emerging at an extraordinary pace, with profound implications for economies, education, science, labour markets, public services and national security. But the risks are equally profound and growing, and so too is public concern.“Today’s political leaders… must make hard choices that will signficantly alter their countries’ trajectories. However, the institutions of the modern state meant to support political leaders in making these choices are simply not equipped for what is coming.”Explore more on these topicsAI (artificial intelligence)NvidiaComputingTechnology sectornewsShareReuse this content

title: Google fined more than €400m by Irish regulator over its use of location data | Google | The Guardian
description: Watchdog says users may have been unaware their information was used to target adverts or infer their interests
Author: Lisa O’Carroll
Headline: Watchdog says users may have been unaware their information was used to target adverts or infer their interests
Content: The DPC found that Google users could have been unaware of how their data was being used.Photograph: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe DPC found that Google users could have been unaware of how their data was being used.Photograph: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg/Getty ImagesGoogleGoogle fined more than €400m by Irish regulator over its use of location dataWatchdog says users may have been unaware their information was used to target adverts or infer their interestsLisa O’CarrollMon 21 Sep 2026 06.57 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGoogle has been fined more than €400m (£345m) over the way it processed users’ location data, following claims that the tech giant had manipulated users into agreeing to be constantly tracked on their mobile phones.The fine, imposed by Ireland’s Data Protection Commission (DPC), comes after complaints from multiple European consumer organisations that Google was following every step users took.Location-related adverts are familiar to holidaymakers, but seven European consumer organisations hadcomplained that undue use of location data can also lead to a breach of privacy.The DPC inquiry was prompted byresearch by the Norwegian consumer agency in 2018which suggested location data could reveal details such as religious beliefs (by tracking places of worship), political leanings (for example knowing a user has gone to demonstrations), health conditions (if a user has gone to hospital) and sexual orientation (if they have gone to certain bars).The DPC launched its inquiry six years ago and set out to find out whether Google had a valid legal basis for its use of location data.It found that Google users could have been unaware that their location was being used to influence them with adverts or to gather details about their health and interests.“Location data is a type of personal data which is processed by way of location tracking, and includes data collected or processed by Google, which by itself or in conjunction with other information an individual’s location can be inferred,” said Graham Doyle, a deputy commissioner at the DPC.“Location data can bring both benefits and harms to individuals.“It can greatly enhance the utility of online services, but it can also reveal a significant amount of information about an individual, including information that is inherently private,” Doyle added.Responding to the DPC’s ruling, a Google spokeperson said: “This case centres around historical policies that have since been updated. From 2019 onwards, we’ve significantly evolved our practices and launched robust tools that make managing location data simple.”The European Consumer Organisation (BEUC) based its complaint on research by the Forbrukerrådet, the Norwegian consumer agency, whichclaimed Google used “various tricks”to ensure location history and web and app activity were enabled.“Today marks an important milestone in the effort to protect our rights online. People must be able to understand what they are agreeing to without being deceived or manipulated into making choices they otherwise would never have made,” says Finn Myrstad, director of digital policy at the Norwegian Consumer Council.BEUC said that geolocation data was “one of the most invasive forms of consumer surveillance”.Agustín Reyna, director general of BEUC, welcomed the ruling but said “the time needed to come to this conclusion is disproportionate with the seriousness of the infringement” arguing “late enforcement can be as harmful as no enforcement at all”.The DPC inquiry looked at “web and app activity”, “location history” and “location accuracy” between 25 May 2018 and 4 February 2020.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionImposing a fine of €403m, the DPC ordered Google to bring its processing into compliance with the EU’s general data protection regulation (GDPR) within six months.It is the fourth-largest fine imposed by the Irish regulator, which has EU-wide responsibility for all the US tech giants with EU headquarters in Ireland.It has previously fined Meta €1.2bn, TikTok €530m and Instagram (also Meta owned) €405m.Doyle said: “The GDPR provides a high level of protection of personal data throughout the EEA, and requires that the processing of personal data must be carried out in a lawful, fair and transparent manner.AI slowdown calls justified but collapse of bubble may be more immediate threat | Heather StewartRead more“As a result of Google’s failures in this regard, individuals could have been unaware that their location was being used to, for example, influence them with ads or to infer their interests, and could lose control over their personal data.“The retention of users’ location data for longer than necessary aggravated this loss of control,” added Doyle.There are three other ongoing statutory large-scale inquiries open that concern Google, all of which are at an advanced stage.Explore more on these topicsGoogleEuropean UnionSmartphonesAlphabetMobile phonesEuropenewsShareReuse this content

title: Halt super-intelligent AI with non-proliferation treaty, Ed Davey to say | Liberal Democrat conference | The Guardian
description: At Lib Dems’ conference in Brighton, leader will accuse Andy Burnham of relying on Donald Trump and ‘tech bros’ to solve problem
Author: Alexandra Topping
Headline: At Lib Dems’ conference in Brighton, leader will accuse Andy Burnham of relying on Donald Trump and ‘tech bros’ to solve problem
Content: Ed Davey on the beach at Brighton during the Lib Dems’ party conference, where he is expected to lay out plans for a new international AI safety agency.Photograph: Phil Lewis/SOPA Images/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenEd Davey on the beach at Brighton during the Lib Dems’ party conference, where he is expected to lay out plans for a new international AI safety agency.Photograph: Phil Lewis/SOPA Images/ShutterstockLiberal Democrat conferenceHalt super-intelligent AI with non-proliferation treaty, Ed Davey to sayAt Lib Dems’ conference in Brighton, leader will accuse Andy Burnham of relying on Donald Trump and ‘tech bros’ to solve problemAlexandra ToppingandPeter WalkerMon 21 Sep 2026 17.30 EDTLast modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEd Davey is to call for a global nuclear-style non-proliferation treaty to halt the development of super-intelligent AI when he makes his keynote speech at theLiberal Democrat conference, accusing Andy Burnham of relying on Donald Trump and “tech bros” to solve the problem.When he addresses the faithful on the final day of the gathering in Brighton, the party leader will
